### #41 Top teams block: build it, and record the 2026-08-10 design (four boards, top 7)

_opened · created 2026-08-10_

Build the **Top teams** block on the home page, and write the 2026-08-10 CPO design decisions
into `docs/wireframes/10_home.md` §0 in the same MR.

⚠ §0's six-board table is SUPERSEDED by this issue. Do the spec edit FIRST, in the same branch, so
the build and the document never diverge. This description is the current design; it REPLACES the
earlier version of this issue rather than layering on it.

## The block

Four boards, in this order. **One metric each. Top 7 teams. All ranked descending.**

| # | Board name | Metric | 
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Goals per match | `goals_per_match` |
| 2 | Shots on target per match | `shots_on_goal_per_match` |
| 3 | Passes per match | `passes_per_match` |
| 4 | Duels per match | `duels_per_match` |

**One metric per row, not two.** CPO 2026-08-10: two metrics per entry *"just brings problems and
makes perceptions complicated"*. Three intermediate designs (two columns, then for/against pairs,
then six boards including the two "against" boards) were tried and rejected in the same session.

What this removes, and it is worth stating because each was a live problem:

- **No column-header row.** With one metric, the board title is the only label the number needs, so
  the header would only repeat it. This kills the title-repeats-header duplication structurally.
- **No `% Pass accuracy`**, so the block no longer depends on a metric that is broken today
  (23–30% since 2022 against 72–73% before; filed on the unreachable GitHub tracker as #841).
- **No `lower_better` metric**, so "all descending" agrees with every board's catalogue
  `direction`. ⚠ Keep it that way: ranking a lower-is-better metric descending puts the WORST
  teams at the top of a block called Top teams. If such a board is ever added, its direction needs
  ruling explicitly.

### ⚠ The board name spells the rate out; it does not carry the sigil

CPO 2026-08-10, in two steps. "Ø Goals" reads badly as a heading — but bare "Goals" is **wrong**,
because these are per-match rates and a bare noun reads as a season total. So the sigil is expanded
into the words it stands for: **`label_en` "Ø Goals" → board name "Goals per match"**.

The expansion is driven by the **metric id**, not by the sigil, and the two are asserted to agree:

- all four rank metric ids end in `_per_match`, which is where " per match" comes from
- "Ø" alone is ambiguous — the catalogue also carries per-90 labels ("Ø Successful dribbles per
  90"), and appending "per match" to one of those would produce nonsense

So the board name still derives from the catalogue and cannot drift from the metric it ranks. This
matters more than it did before: with no column header, **the title is the only label the number
carries anywhere on the page.**

⚠ Applies per locale. The Finnish labels carry "Ø" too, so the name must be derived from the
localised label ("Ø Maalit"), never from the English one.

## Shared display rules

- **Top 7 per board** — raised from 5, CPO 2026-08-10. ⚠ **This applies to Top players too**
  (#40 updated), so §0's "Top 5 entries per board" line must change for BOTH blocks.
- **Every row carries the team AND its league.** A pooled board ranks across seven leagues, so the
  club no longer implies the competition.
- **⚠ The team name must never truncate.** The design system ellipsises `.nm`, which is right on a
  fixture card and wrong here: a clipped name defeats a block whose whole purpose is to send people
  to the team page. Names wrap and the row grows. The single-column layout gives the name about
  200px at 375px, so this is comfortable rather than tight.
- **⚠ The board title must not truncate either**, for the same reason and more sharply — it is now
  the only label the value has.
- **A metric with no value is HIDDEN, not dashed** (§0), and with one metric per board that means
  **the whole board is omitted**. ⚠ **RULED 2026-08-10: a board with no data is simply not
  rendered** — no placeholder, no empty state, no "data unavailable" message. CPO: *"if a board is
  missing, the user may not even notice, so don't show."* Surviving boards keep their order and
  nothing reflows to fill the gap; the block renders with however many boards have data. If none
  do, the block itself does not render.
- ⚠ **Consequence for the PIPELINE, not the page.** A silently omitted board is invisible to the
  visitor by design — and therefore invisible to us too. A DQ check has to catch a board that
  vanished, because the page deliberately will not. Data quality is non-negotiable here and the
  CPO cannot verify numbers by hand, so silence on the page must not mean silence everywhere.
- Every row links out. That is why the block exists.

Superseded and no longer in force for this block: "two value columns per board" and "each label
centred above its own number, as a table header". Both were written for the multi-metric design.

## Layout

One column of boards, full content width — the two-column split was tried and rejected on the
player block.

Each board is: rank · crest · team (name + league) · value, right-aligned. Right alignment matches
`.pstat` in the design system; the earlier centring existed only to pair a value with the header
above it.

⚠ **The name and its league line share ONE line where there is room and STACK where there is not —
but the decision is PER BOARD, never per row** (CPO 2026-08-10: *"they all stack together or
not"*). Applies to both blocks; on Top players the second line is club · league.

A first version used `flex-wrap`, which decides per row: one board rendered rows 1, 5 and 6 inline
and rows 2, 3, 4 and 7 stacked — correct for each row, ragged as a block. CSS cannot ask whether a
SIBLING wrapped, so the trigger has to be something every row shares: **the board's own width, via a
container query** (`.board` already declares `container-type: inline-size`). `flex-wrap: nowrap`
above the threshold is what enforces it — without it a single over-long row could still wrap alone
and bring the raggedness back. The cell needs `min-width: 0`, or a long name widens the row instead
of wrapping inside it.

⚠ This reintroduces a chosen number, which the per-row version avoided. It is **480px**, derived
rather than guessed. Fixed chrome is `18 rank + 24 crest + 64 value + 36 gaps = 142px`, so the name
cell gets `board - 142px`, and 480 gives it 338px. Widest rows: the player row "Bruno Fernandes" +
"Manchester United · Premier League" needs ~331px (→ a ~473px board); the team row "Brighton & Hove
Albion" + "Premier League" needs ~275px (→ ~417px). **480 clears both**, so one number serves the
two blocks. A 375px phone (343px board) stacks; a 680px content column (624px board) stays inline.

⚠ An earlier 560px was too high and pushed a normal desktop width into the stacked branch. Note the
threshold has to satisfy the LONGER of the two blocks, because they share this CSS but not their
content — the player second line is "club · league", the team one is just the league.

**Better for the real build:** the site is static, so the component knows the actual strings at
build time and can choose stacked-or-inline per board from the DATA, with no threshold at all.

The board head mirrors `.fxgroup > .gh`, which Next matches already uses on this page, so the two
blocks read as siblings rather than introducing a per-page treatment.

### The crest slot

Every row carries the **club crest image** — the team logo, on player rows as well as team rows
(CPO 2026-08-10).

⚠ **The design system's text-initials fallback is NOT the intended look.** `.crest` in `system.css`
is an image box that falls back to bold initials, and in review the mock rendered "RMA", "BAY",
"MCI" because it cannot fetch crests. On a player row those initials merely restate the club already
written in the sub-line, and it reads as if the abbreviation were the design. The mock now draws a
neutral placeholder instead. Keep the initials fallback for a row whose crest is genuinely missing;
do not ship it as the normal case.

⚠ **This block inherits #36.** Crests are hotlinked from `media.api-sports.io`, 24 per locale, which
is a go-live blocker with a licence question attached. The block does not add to that problem, but
it does depend on it being solved.

Implementation notes, all re-confirmed building the mock:

- **`repeat(var(--n), …)` is invalid CSS.** The repeat count must be a literal integer; a custom
  property there silently invalidates the whole `grid-template-columns` declaration. Write the
  track list out WHOLE and read it with `var()` as the ENTIRE value.
- **The value column must be a fixed width, never `auto`.** With one column the trap is milder but
  not gone: `auto` lets a 3-digit value ("682") size its track differently from a 2-digit one, so
  the numbers stop aligning down the board.
- **Each board must be its own container** (`container-type: inline-size`), so measurements resolve
  against the board and not the page. Sizing to the page breaks when the content column is capped
  narrower than the viewport.
- ⚠ **Stacking must blockify the CHILDREN, not just the cell.** `.nm` and `.sub` carry no
  `display` of their own, because the inline branch is flex and flex blockifies its children. A
  stacked branch that sets `display: block` only on the cell therefore leaves two INLINE spans that
  run straight together — "Bayern MünchenBundesliga". This shipped and was visible in review; every
  other CSS assertion passed on it, because none of them checked that stacking actually stacks.

## What this needs from the warehouse

**Exactly four metrics**, all `entity = team`:

`goals_per_match` · `shots_on_goal_per_match` · `passes_per_match` · `duels_per_match`

⚠ **Re-scope GAP-29 to this list** (`docs/wireframes/99_gaps_register.md`) — it was written against

`int_team_season__metrics_cumulative`; what does not exist is top-N-per-metric ACROSS teams.

No longer used by this block: `points_capture`, `points_won`, `deserved_points`,

`finishing_efficiency`, `defensive_actions_per_match`, `key_passes_per_match`, `pass_accuracy`,
`duels_won_pct`.

⚠ **Deserved-vs-actual was considered and dropped.** Deserved points needs ONE ladder to mean
anything, so it is a within-league number and a board pooling seven leagues cannot carry it. This

## Pools, scope and selection

Unchanged from §0 and still live:

### #50 "Next matches" content block: one standard for every surface (competition, then date)

_opened · created 2026-08-10_

**Designed and CPO-reviewed 2026-08-10.** This issue is the standard. Build from here.

The same content was being rendered five different ways. This defines it once so every surface
that shows upcoming matches uses it unchanged.

## What it replaces

| Surface | What it renders today |
|---|---|
| `home/HeroFixtures.astro` | `.fxrow` grouped by competition |
| `team/TeamFixtures.astro` | `.nextfx` — a bespoke single-match card |
| `fixture/RecentMatch.astro`, `team/TeamFixtureRow.astro` | `.rmatch` — written from one team's point of view |
| the competition-hub and Matches mocks | a fourth and fifth treatment, added this week |

⚠ **`.nextfx` retires.** A next match is the first row, not a special card.

## The block

**Two levels of grouping, always in this order: competition, then date. Then rows.**

```
[logo] Bundesliga                          <- level 1, links to the competition hub
  FRI 28 FEB                               <- level 2
    [crest] Bayern München                        20:30
    [crest] VfB Stuttgart                          CET
  SAT 1 MAR
    ...
```

### Anatomy — every value comes from a column

| Element | Level | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Competition logo | 1 | `dim_league.league_logo_url` |
| Competition name | 1 | `dim_league.league_name` |
| Competition link | 1 | registry `slug` |
| Date | 2 | `fct_fixture.kickoff_datetime`, venue-local |
| Club crest / national flag | row | `dim_team.team_logo_url` |
| Club or country name | row | `dim_team.team_name` |
| Kick-off | row | `fct_fixture.kickoff_datetime`, venue-local |
| Timezone | row | ⚠ **not derivable yet** — see below |
| Match link | row | registry `slug` + fixture slug |

**Nothing is hard-coded.** The CPO's words: *"This content block draws from a data model, meaning
nothing should be hard-coded at all. All data should come from the table being used."*

## Rules that never vary

1. **Competition, then date.** Never day-then-competition on one surface and matchday on another.
2. **No matchday on the heading.** It belongs on the match page — and the warehouse only holds the
   provider's raw `"Regular Season - 25"`, which shipped untranslated to all three locales once
   already (**#866**). Turning it into a phase plus a number is taxonomy mapping, which the
   consumption layer forbids.
3. **The competition heading is unmissable** — 17px name, 26px logo, a full-weight rule and real
   space above the group. CPO: *"you scroll down and barely notice that the competition has
   changed."*
4. **One row component**, and no surface may restyle it.
5. **The two sides stack**, each with its badge; the kick-off has its own column.
6. **The timezone is on EVERY row.** Never on a heading.
7. **The name never truncates.** `system.css` ellipsises this slot; the block overrides it.
8. **A national side gets a flag, not a crest** — a different asset, not the same one restyled.
9. **Every row links to its match.** A row that cannot link is not shown here.

## ⭐ The rule that took two rounds to get right

**A level may be OMITTED when the page already supplies it. It may never be MOVED.**

- The **competition page drops level 1** — the competition is its `<h1>`, and an earlier version
  rendered "Bundesliga" as a group heading directly beneath "Bundesliga".
- What is forbidden is the same fact appearing in **different slots on different surfaces**. The
  timezone sat on the group heading for single-country leagues and on the row for the rest, which
  put two shapes of one block on one screen.

## What adapts to the surface

| Surface | Competitions | Which matches | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Home | many | the next N across all competitions | — |
| Matches | many | each competition's next matchday | no cap |
| Competition page | one | that competition's next matchday | **level 1 dropped** |
| Club page | one | that club's next match | not built. ⚠ Open: does one row still carry level 1? |

**Window rule (CPO):** *"every next match (in terms of next match day) from the competitions we
have in the data, but not the matches after that"* — a match beyond the next round has nothing
meaningful to send a reader to. So the window is **per competition**, not a date range.

**Past matches never appear** on a next-matches surface. They have their own view.

## ⚠ One value the block cannot render honestly yet

**The venue-local timezone.** `fct_fixture.kickoff_timezone` exists, but every kickoff in the
committed data is `+00:00` — it is the provider's **request** zone, not the venue's.

- For a single-country league the registry's `country` supplies it — 10 of the 12 active.
- **MLS and Liga MX span several zones** (four in the US, three in Mexico) and need the venue's own.

Until that lands those two render a dash. **This is the one thing blocking the block from being
correct**, and it is warehouse work, not frontend.

## Also inherited

- **#36** — the club crest and now the league logo are both hot-linked from `media.api-sports.io`.
  Adding the logo creates no new problem but raises the count on a go-live blocker.
- **League name has TWO sources today.** `export_site_data.py:821` reads `dim_league` for the
  fixture page; `:609` reads the registry everywhere else, and the registry's is the legal form
  ("1. Fußball-Bundesliga"), which the CPO rejected. **One source: `dim_league`, corrections in

### #100 10_home.md's supersession layering has cost two MRs five review rounds each - reduce it to the current design

_opened · created 2026-09-02_

`docs/wireframes/10_home.md` has cost **two separate MRs five review rounds each**, for the same
structural reason both times. This is a defect in the document, not in either change.

## The evidence

| | `10_home.md` | next largest wireframe |
|---|---|---|
| lines | **887** | 319 (`metrics_display.md`) |
| strikethrough markers (`~~`) | **87** | — |
| "SUPERSEDED" | 21 | — |
| "DROPPED" | 22 | — |
| "VOID" | 12 | — |
| "withdrawn" | 7 | — |

It is **2.8x the next largest** spec and carries 87 struck passages. A single fact can be asserted,
struck, re-asserted and re-struck in six places.

## What it has cost, twice

**The file's own header records the first instance**, about a different stale claim:

> "Five rounds of review were needed to find them all, because they were fixed one reported
> instance at a time instead of swept as a class - S1, S3, S4, S6, S8 and this header all carried
> the same stale claim."

**!142 then repeated it exactly.** Three lines of SQL (`mart_leaderboards`: add the assists board,
add four club columns) took **five review rounds and two CPO round-cap overrides**. The model diff
was byte-identical from round 1 and passed every round. **Every FAIL was a stale sentence in this
file.** Four sweeps failed four different ways:

1. searched the STRING changed ("9 count boards") rather than the CLAIM falsified - the stale
   statements are phrased as absences ("STILL MISSING", "not selected", "none of it built") and
   share no vocabulary with a board count
2. searched only where a reviewer had already pointed, not the class
3. case-sensitive ("None of it is built" vs "none of it built")
4. **line-based** - the last instance straddles a line break (`none of it\nbuilt`), so no line grep
   can match it, including the reviewer's own quoted string

## Why the file causes this

The document is written as an **append-only record of supersessions** rather than a statement of
the current design. Every ruling is layered on top of the last, struck in place. That is deliberate
and it has real value - the history is auditable - but it has two consequences:

- **The same fact lives in many places** with different phrasings and different strike states, so
  correcting it is a sweep rather than an edit.
- **Disclaimers do not compose.** The file carries at least three ("S0 is the current authority",
  "everything below this line describes the removed module", "the register is the authority - check
  it, not this summary"), each correctly scoped to a different region. Three review rounds were
  spent establishing which disclaimer reached which sentence.

## Proposed disposition

Reduce `10_home.md` to **the current design**, and move the supersession history out.

- the current composition is three blocks: next matches (built), Top players, Top teams
- git holds every superseded ruling losslessly; `escalations.log` holds the rulings themselves
- keep exactly one authority statement, not three
- the gaps belong to `99_gaps_register.md`, which is already the authority for them and is kept
  current - the file's own S10 list duplicates it and goes stale independently

Not proposed as a rewrite of the design. The design is settled; only the document is the problem.

## Notes

- This is filed as a **process/doc-health issue**, not blocking any build. But it taxes every Home
  MR until it is done, and the next two are already queued (GAP-28 the authored pool field, GAP-29
  the team boards mart), both of which will touch this file's warehouse-needs section again.
- The sweep method that finally worked, worth reusing on any doc of this shape: read each file
  whole, **collapse all whitespace**, match case-insensitively for the CLAIM in every phrasing
  including negations, then adjudicate every hit in writing. Run that way it returned **38 hits
  tree-wide, of which exactly 1 was genuine**. A sweep is only trustworthy if it is allowed to
  return mostly noise.
- Related: **#71** (stale-claim check - a correction lands in one artifact and the superseded claim
  survives in another). This issue is a concrete, measured instance of that class.

### #101 Home: which competition_group a render uses, and how it rotates when a group is out of season

_opened · created 2026-09-02_

Home's **Top players** and **Top teams** blocks each show *one entry per league*, drawn from a set of
leagues. GAP-28 gives every domestic league a `competition_group`, so the sets now exist:

| group | n | leagues |
|---|---|---|
| `elite` | 7 | Premier League · La Liga · Bundesliga · Serie A · Ligue 1 · Liga Portugal · Eredivisie |
| `europe` | 3 | Belgian Pro League · Süper Lig · Ekstraklasa |
| `international` | 2 | Liga MX · Saudi Pro League |
| `calendar` | 6 | Brasileirão · Primera División · MLS · J1 League · K League 1 · Veikkausliiga |
| `secondary` | 1 | 2. Bundesliga |

**What is not decided is which group a given page render uses.**

## The CPO's steer

> "Top 7 definitely for the home page (but I would like to have a mechanism for showing the others
> as well, by rotation or randomly, no idea, especially when a league group is not active but
> another is -> file it, should not block us here)"

And, on what a board may contain:

> "It uses group 1, or groups 2 and 3 merged (so one board for 2 and 3). Or it can show group 4"

So the candidate selections are:

- `elite`
- `europe` + `international` **merged into one board**
- `calendar`

`secondary` is never a home-page candidate.

## The real problem: seasonality

The groups are not simultaneously in season, and that is the reason this is not just a preference:

- `elite`, `europe` and `international` run **split-year** seasons — roughly August to May
- `calendar` runs **calendar-year** seasons — roughly February to November

So in June and July, the split-year groups have no current-season data worth ranking, while
`calendar` is mid-season. A home page hardcoded to `elite` is empty for two months of the year; one
hardcoded to `calendar` is wrong for the other ten.

⚠ This is exactly the case the CPO named: *"especially when a league group is not active but another
is"*.

## Open questions

1. **What drives the choice** — a fixed rotation, randomness, or a rule keyed on which groups
   actually have current-season data? The third is the only one that solves the seasonality problem
   rather than working around it.
2. **What counts as "in season"** for a group. Needs a definition against the warehouse (finished
   fixtures in the current season? a minimum count, like the `>= 3 finished games` gate the
   benchmark models already use?), not a date range hardcoded in the frontend.
3. **Whether the choice is per-render or per-build.** The site is static, so "random" means random
   at build time and identical for every visitor until the next build. That may be fine, but it is a
   different thing from what "random" usually implies and should be stated.
4. **Whether both blocks always show the same group.** Top players and Top teams could diverge —
   probably shouldn't, but it has not been ruled.
5. **How the choice is surfaced to the reader.** A board titled the same while its underlying league
   set silently changed is a display-honesty problem; the block may need to say which leagues it is
   ranking across. Note the mock's intro line already names its leagues in page copy.

## Notes

- **Not blocking.** GAP-28 ships the data; GAP-29 (the team boards mart) is next. Both blocks can be
  built against `elite` alone and this decided afterwards — that is the CPO's stated preference.
- Whatever is decided must live in the warehouse or the export, not as a literal in a component:
  the consumption-layer contract says the export may select and filter but never derive, and a
  hardcoded league list in Astro would be the third copy of a fact the registry already owns.
- Related: **#40** (Top players), **#41** (Top teams), **GAP-28**/**GAP-29** in
  `docs/wireframes/99_gaps_register.md`.

### #127 Home: recheck and approve the design, data sources and links

_opened · created 2026-09-12_

**Requested by:** Rami

## What exactly

- [ ] A review of **Home**, for the CPO to approve on this issue before anything is built or rebuilt:
  1. what is on the page, block by block, in plain words;
  2. where each block's data comes from — a warehouse model, or a named gap where nothing serves it yet;
  3. which hub reaches the page, and what the page links on to.
- [ ] The approved design is recorded here, in this issue, and the design chain (`docs/wireframes/00_overview.md`) points at it. Nothing about the page is settled anywhere else.
- [ ] Build issues are filed against this one only once the design is approved.

**State today:** built with three blocks (next matches, top players, top teams); the menu items lead nowhere; the mock generator still renders a dropped fourth block.

## Why

The roadmap is the site's menu, in order, each hub before the pages behind it, and every page rechecked by the CPO — built or not — because the earlier agreements may be stale and a built page is not a proof it can be built to the current design. One issue per page is the single place where its design, its data sources and its links are agreed.

## How

1. Put the current state in front of the CPO: the built page in the browser, or the wireframe rendered, with the data source beside every block.
2. He approves, changes or strikes, one page at a time.
3. Record the outcome here; correct or retire whatever document disagrees with it in the same MR that builds it.

---

## The approved design (CPO rulings, 2026-09-12 and 2026-09-13)

Consolidated from the review notes below this description. Where a note and this section disagree, this section is current.

### Menu (header), six items

Competitions → the competitions index (built). **Matches, Teams, Players, Standings, Leaderboards → their index pages**, none of which exists yet; each link goes live when its milestone builds the page. **Stats is renamed Leaderboards** (menu, footer, milestone 7, issues #139/#140). A further item (Analytics or Predictions) was mentioned, not ruled.

### Block 1 — Next matches

- **Shows:** every competition with an upcoming matchday, always — on Monday the Bundesliga already shows next weekend's round. A competition leaves the block only when it has no fixture not yet started. All ingested competitions, cups included.
- **Window: each competition's next matchday**, not a calendar day — the round (the fixture's round name) of its earliest fixture not yet started. Bundesliga: Friday to Sunday, nine matches.
- **Per competition: 3 visible, the rest folded** under a "show all" on the block; the 3 are the earliest kickoffs. No JavaScript needed for the fold.
- **Order of competitions:** the shared key of 2026-08-16/18 stands — the day the matchday starts, then region rank (Europe first), then kickoff, then code. Soonest first: a cup playing Tuesday sits above the weekend leagues. Rows inside a competition by kickoff. Times in UTC, 24-hour, with the date. One line of text when nothing is upcoming.
- **Data:** `marts.mart_next_matchday` (every competition's next round, served by the warehouse — CPO 2026-09-13 on #143, "Path A"; closes GAP-32), `core.dim_team`, `marts.mart_competition_index` (display name, region rank).
- **Links:** competition heading → the competition hub; match row → the match page. Both built.
- **Considered, not taken:** a 3-day calendar window (246 rows on a weekend, measured); filter buttons by competition and date on the block. Both belong to the Matches page.

### Block 2 — Top players

- **Pool:** the seven `elite` leagues until **#101** (the per-build group rotation) is built. Rotation weights changed to **80 elite / 10 europe+international merged / 10 calendar**; #101 is the build item and carries the scope and the season trap.
- **Boards:** Goals, Assists, Passes, Key passes, in that order (ruled 2026-08-10, confirmed). One metric per board, the title is the catalogue name, one value column, club crest on the row, most first. 7 rows, one per league; a tie inside a league goes to fewer minutes.
- **Intro line kept:** "Current season. The top player from each league in the rankings: …", naming the leagues, as #101 requires.
- **Data:** `marts.mart_leaderboards`, joined to the registry seed for the group.
- **Links:** row → the player's page `/{lang}/players/{player}/` (a placeholder today; the real page is the Players milestone). **Metric name → the Leaderboards page** (#139), from which the reader reaches player and team leaderboards, defined at that review.

### Block 3 — Top teams

- **Pool, intro line, rotation:** as block 2, same group each build.
- **Boards:** Goals per match, Shots on goal per match, Passes per match, Duels per match, in that order (confirmed). One decimal for the first two, whole numbers for the last two, from the catalogue.
- **No minimum games.** `mart_team_leaderboards` drops its `season_games_played >= 3` gate; a team ranks from its first finished game. The benchmark models' own gate and #101's slot eligibility are separate rules, untouched.
- **Tie on a rate:** broken on the underlying total (more goals at the same rate); `team_sk` last. Recorded on **#114**, which is the build item.
- **Data:** `marts.mart_team_leaderboards`, same registry join.
- **Links:** row → the team's page `/{lang}/teams/{team}/` (built). Metric name → the Leaderboards page, as block 2.

### Footer

Competitions, Teams, Players, Leaderboards → the same index pages as the header, live when built. **About and Imprint are go-live items** (with the legal pages, the domain, dropping `noindex`); no go-live issue exists yet.

### Links into Home

The brand mark in header and footer on every page; the "Home" breadcrumb on the competition hub, match, team, player and competitions-index pages. Unchanged.

### Documents this supersedes

`docs/wireframes/10_home.md` (the one-day window in §5, the unlinked board titles) and `design-mocks/gen_home.py` (still renders the dropped Browse block). Both are corrected in the MR that builds against this issue.

### Build items filed or owned elsewhere

#101 (rotation, 80/10/10), #114 (team tie-break), #139 (Leaderboards hub). The Home-only work — matchday window and fold, header and footer links, metric-name links, the no-floor change, the two document fixes — is filed against this issue once ticked.

### #145 One data-backed sentence per page: the template generator in the export, and each page's wording

_opened · created 2026-09-14_

**Requested by:** Rami

The one data-backed sentence per page that `docs/site_architecture.md` §6 has required since the architecture was written ("short, metric-backed sentences generated at build time per page; honest only — generated from real mart values, skipped when data is insufficient; generator lives in the export layer"). Nothing has been built for it; no page carries one. CPO 2026-09-14, at the competition page review: start with template sentences on every page; the AI-written intro is a later, separate decision.

## What exactly

- [ ] The export fills one sentence per page from that page's served numbers and names, in each of the three languages, from a template that lives with the site's other copy (`site_v2/src/i18n/strings.ts`, placeholders like the existing `{n}` / `{leagues}` keys), and writes NOTHING for a page whose template has a missing input — never a partial sentence, never a fabricated number.
- [ ] Every number and name in a rendered sentence is a value the page's payload already carries; a test fails on a template placeholder with no served source.
- [ ] Each page kind's sentence — which facts, which wording — is decided by the CPO at that page's review or, for pages already approved (Home #127, Competitions hub #128), on this issue before it is built. First: the competition page's league sentence (drafted on #47 / #129: "**{leader}** lead after {played} matches, {gap} points clear of **{second}**."); cups and group stages get a template of their own or nothing.
- [ ] Home carries a sentence; its facts and wording are decided here (candidates: the count of matches and competitions on the next matchday; the leagues the boards cover). Approved as an addition to #127's design when decided.

## Why

Every page except the fixture page is a list of numbers; a sentence made from them is what keeps a page from being thin for search and gives the reader the point of the page in one line. Templates do this with no running cost and no wrong fact; an AI-written version is a separate decision with a cost line (see the exploration detail).

## How

1. One function in `scripts/export_site_data.py` (`sentence(kind, lang, values)`) that resolves a template key per page kind and locale, substitutes named placeholders, and returns `None` when any placeholder's value is missing; the export writes the result into each page's payload under one key.
2. Templates as `strings.ts` keys per page kind (EN/DE/FI), through the copy gate like every other string.
3. A test per template that every placeholder is a served field of that page's payload, and that a missing value yields no sentence.
4. The competition page's league template first; Home's when its wording is ruled here.
5. Evidence from the built pages: the sentence rendered in three languages, and a page with thin data rendering none.

**Not in scope:** AI-written intros (own issue, own cost line); sentences for pages whose reviews have not happened (match, team, player); any sentence on a cup or group table until a template is ruled.

<details>
<summary>Exploration detail — for the builder and the reviewers, not required reading</summary>

- The template on the mock (`design-mocks/gen_competition_hub.py`, `LEDE_EN` / `LEDE_FI`) uses four `mart_standings` columns: the rank-1 team name, its `played`, the points gap to rank 2, the rank-2 team name. A German version is not drafted.
- AI-written intros, costed 2026-09-14 for the CPO: one short call per page and language; ~300 pages × 3 languages today, a full regeneration ≈ $2–5 (Sonnet 5) or $5–15 (Opus 5) at list price, half via the batch endpoint, cents to a few dollars a night with change detection; build effort one to two weeks mostly on guards (no number or name not in the input, skip on thin data, cache keyed on the data, sampled review). A new mechanism and a recurring cost — the CPO's decision, deferred.
- The Home review (#127) did not raise the sentence; the built Home has none. Recorded here rather than as a #127 amendment so the wording is ruled with the mechanism.
</details>

### #146 Kick-off in the venue's clock: a time zone per venue in the warehouse, a zone label on every fixture row

_opened · created 2026-09-14_

**Requested by:** Rami

CPO 2026-09-14, at the competition page review (#129): kick-off times are shown in the **venue's clock** with a zone label on every row ("20:30 CET", "20:00 BST", "20:00 EDT"), and the date as a heading per day, on every page that lists matches (Home's Next matches block and the competition page share the row; the Matches page will too). The site shows UTC today and no page can do otherwise: nothing in the warehouse says where a match is played in time.

## What exactly

- [ ] Every upcoming fixture row the site renders carries a served local kick-off time and a served zone label (`kickoff_local`, `kickoff_zone_label`), computed in the warehouse from the fixture's venue; the site prints them and converts nothing.
- [ ] A venue has a time zone: a warehouse table of venues (2,492 distinct venue ids on `stg_apif__fixtures_next` today) with an IANA zone derived from the venue's city and country, tested not-null for every venue a fixture references.
- [ ] A fixture with no venue (18,238 of 64,552 today — qualifiers and cups mostly) falls back to its competition's zone from the registry, and the row still shows a zone label; a fixture with neither shows UTC and says so.
- [ ] `mart_next_matchday` (and the fixture-page payload) serve the two columns; Home and the competition page render them; the date heading per day uses the local date.

## Why

The CPO ruled the venue's clock: it is what the club, the league and the TV listing print, so the site never contradicts them, and it is the same for every reader with no script. The reader converts to their own time; a label on every row makes that honest.

## How

1. Measure how far city + country resolves to one zone for the 2,492 venues (a country with one zone is the bulk; the US, Brazil, Mexico, Russia, Australia need the city).
2. A seed or a base model mapping venue → IANA zone; a not-null test over every referenced venue; the registry gains a fallback zone per competition (one field, the mock's `ZONE` table is the draft).
3. `fct_fixture` (or the mart) computes `kickoff_local` and the zone's abbreviation for that date (CET/CEST, GMT/BST — daylight time changes the label) in SQL.
4. The export carries both; `FixtureRow.astro` prints them; the date heading per day replaces the per-row date on Home and the competition page.
5. Tests: a known fixture in each of five zones renders the expected label; a no-venue fixture falls back; a no-zone fixture shows UTC.

**Not in scope:** the reader's-clock script (ruled out 2026-09-14); results rows (cut from the competition page 2026-08-10).

<details>
<summary>Exploration detail — for the builder and the reviewers, not required reading</summary>

- The provider's `fixture.timezone` is `UTC` on every row because the ingest requests UTC; it is not the venue's zone.
- The design mocks (`design-mocks/gen_block_standard.py`) carry a hand-typed per-competition zone (`ZONE`: BL1 CET, PL GMT, VL EET, SPL AST; MLS and LMX `None` because they span zones) and the mock row shows `time + zone`; that table is the draft of the registry fallback, not a source.
- Daylight time: the label must be computed per kick-off date, not stored per venue (BigQuery `FORMAT_DATETIME('%Z', DATETIME(ts, zone))` gives the abbreviation).
- The three options put to the CPO: UTC (today), the venue's clock, the reader's clock via a script (the architecture's §6 note); the venue's clock was chosen.
</details>

### #44 Browse: flatten to one row of competition chips, drop the by-competition / by-country split

_opened · created 2026-08-10_

Flatten the home page's **Browse** block to a single row of competition chips: the section head,
then one chip per competition, nothing else.

⚠ **Do NOT touch !27.** That MR is done and awaiting merge; this is a follow-up, agreed as such by
the CPO on 2026-08-10.

## Why

The block currently offers two axes — **by competition** and **by country** — and they list the
**same twelve competitions**. Every competition the registry marks `status: active` is a
`domestic_league`, so the country axis is the competition axis again with a country heading above
each entry. CPO: *"the browse section is repetitive, no need to put by country, by competition —
just browse and then multiple buttons to click on."*

Nothing becomes unreachable. Both axes already reached the same twelve targets.

## What changes

`site_v2/src/components/home/BrowseGrid.astro` renders one `.linkrow` of `.linkchip`, and drops the
`.colhead` / `.subhead` scaffolding entirely.

⚠ **This does NOT make anything unreachable, and it is NOT a strike against !27's acceptance
criterion 2.** That criterion — *"every competition can be browsed two ways"* — is scoped to one
block, and that is too narrow a place to settle reachability. CPO, 2026-08-10: *"on the whole
website it may be browsed in multiple ways."* Reachability is a property of the SITE, so the home
page does not have to carry two axes by itself.

⚠ **Do not re-derive a reachability rule inside this issue.** It belongs to **#45** (internal linking), which is where the question "how many ways can a competition be reached, and from where"
actually gets answered.

## Two things to decide before building

1. **Display names.** The chips take the registry's `name` field, which gives
   "1. Fußball-Bundesliga", "2. Fußball-Bundesliga" and "Major League Soccer". On a chip row those
   read long next to "Serie A" and "Ligue 1". Decide whether browse shows a shorter display name —
   and if so, where it lives, because inventing one in the component would put a naming decision in
   the frontend.
2. **Chips as links.** The CPO: *"it's fine if they redirect to the leagues."* ⚠ The shipped
   component deliberately emits `<span>`, not `<a>`: the competition hub (`/{locale}/{slug}/`) does
   not exist yet, so an anchor today is a guaranteed 404 behind every chip on the home page. The
   existing comment already records the plan — they become links in the PR that ships the hub, and
   `system.css` scopes the hover affordance to `a.linkchip`, so **the tag swap is the whole edit**.
   So either flatten now and keep `<span>`, or gate this on the hub. It does not need to be one MR.

## Do not leave the country axis behind in the payload

⚠ **A deleted module leaves traces that do not carry its name** — that trap fired five times on !27.
The country axis is not only markup:

- `scripts/export_site_data.py:570-596` builds a `countries` axis (`countries.setdefault(...)`, then
  a `"countries": [...]` key) alongside the grouped one.
- `site_v2/src/lib/types.ts:289` types it: `countries: { country: string; competitions: … }[]`.
- `BrowseGrid.astro:57` is the only consumer.

If the axis goes and nothing else reads `countries`, the payload key, its type and the export code
that builds it go with it. **Check for other consumers before deleting.**

⚠ **Delete it; do not park it "for later".** CPO 2026-08-10: *"we don't need countries as entities
because the number of competitions doesn't call for it now. We can add later, if we add at all."*
Countries are ruled out as an entity (see #45), so nothing downstream is waiting on this key.
Scaffolding kept against a maybe reads as a live feature to the next person.

## SEO

The twelve link targets are unchanged, and today they are not links at all — `index.spec.json`
declares `seo.links = { "inbound_hub": "none", "outbound": ["fixture"] }`, so browse contributes
**no outbound edge** while its chips are `<span>`. When they become anchors, that declaration gains
a `competition` edge and the spec must be updated in the same MR.

Removing the country axis removes the only place a country name appears on the home page, and that
is fine: **countries are ruled out as an entity** (#45, CPO 2026-08-10), so there is no country hub
for this block to feed and nothing is left orphaned.

## Blocked by / notes

- Best done AFTER !27 merges, so the two do not conflict on the same component.
- GitLab CI minutes are exhausted (`ci_quota_exceeded`), so nothing can be verified in a pipeline
  yet.
- Reviewed against a composed home-page mock on 2026-08-10 (next matches → Top players → Top teams
  → browse). The CPO also confirmed there that **the page is not too long** at top 7, which closes
  that open item on #40 and #41.

### #47 Competition hub /{locale}/{competition-slug}/ - build it, and record the 2026-08-10 design (next matches, then table)

_opened · created 2026-08-10_

Build the competition hub: `/{locale}/{competition-slug}/`, e.g. `/en/bundesliga/`.

**Designed and CPO-reviewed 2026-08-10.** This issue is the design record; build from here, not
from a wireframe file (`docs/wireframes/04_competition_hub.md` was never written).

## Why this page, before any other

Not because of the browse chips. **Both shipped page specs already declare an `inbound_hub` that
resolves to nothing:**

- `site_v2/src/specs/teams/team.spec.json:12` — `"inbound_hub": "competition"`
- `site_v2/src/specs/competition/matches/fixture.spec.json:12` — `"inbound_hub": "competition"`

So every team page and every fixture page is a declared orphan in fact. The hub is an outstanding
promise, not new scope. It is also the missing middle of the site: today nothing sits between the
home page and a club or a match.

## URL — already settled, and two docs disagree

`docs/site_architecture.md:44-45` settles it:

```
/{locale}/{competition-slug}/                 competition hub (current season)
/{locale}/{competition-slug}/{season-slug}/   competition season archive
```

⚠ `docs/content_architecture.md:48` contradicts this — it gives the competition entity the URL
`/bundesliga/2025-26` with page-count driver "competitions × seasons". **§3 wins**: a permanent
URL per competition accumulates equity instead of splitting it across seasons, which is what every
comparable site does. **Fix `content_architecture.md:48` as part of this work** — leaving two
answers in two authoritative docs is how the wrong one gets built next time.

Route: `site_v2/src/pages/[lang]/[competition]/index.astro`. The `[competition]` param already
exists (the fixture page resolves it via `site_v2/src/data/competitions.json`).

## Composition — TWO blocks, in this order

CPO order, 2026-08-10: **next matches, then the table.**

### Header
- `<h1>` = the registry `name` verbatim ("1. Fußball-Bundesliga"). The formal name is right on the
  competition's own page, whatever browse does with shorter names (#44).
- Meta line: country · tier · season.
- **No competition crest or logo** — we hold none, and a placeholder would be an invented asset.
- **No season selector** — this URL is the current season and there are no archive pages for a
  switcher to reach. Adding the control before its targets exist is the browse-chip 404 again.
- A data-to-text line: *"**Bayern München** lead after 24 matches, 7 points clear of **Bayer 04
  Leverkusen**."* Required by `site_architecture.md` §6 (anti-thin-content), generated in the
  export; every fact in it is a `mart_standings` column.

### Block 1 — Matchday schedule (`core:fct_fixture`)
- The next round's fixtures. **Every row links to its fixture page.**
- The last round's results underneath, with scores. **These rows are INERT.**
  ⚠ Not a design choice: `fetch_fixture_payloads` exports only upcoming fixtures, so a played
  match has no page to link to (the fixture spec declares `url_permanence: ephemeral`, #861).
  They become links the day that is fixed.
- Winner shown by tone and weight, never by hue — green stays reserved for "better value", red for
  a Loss pill.
- Reuses `.fxgroup` / `.fxrow` from the home page's fixtures hero verbatim. Two additions: the
  whole row is an anchor, and a played row carries goals.
- ⚠ Cutting the results group makes the page strictly "next matches" — a one-line change if
  wanted.

### Block 2 — League / group table (`mart_standings`)
- **All rows. Every team name is an anchor.** This is the reachability payload and the team
  directory in one, and it is what discharges `inbound_hub: "competition"` for every team page.
- Columns: # · crest · club · P · W · D · L · GD · Pts. W/D/L hide below a 470px container; the
  rest stay.
- ⚠ **The name must never truncate** — `system.css` ellipsises `.nm` and the table overrides it.
- "**Table**" is the display name; `mart_standings` is the data name. `site_architecture.md:46`
  already reserves `/{competition-slug}/table/` and `content_architecture.md:78` already calls the
  block "League / group table". "Standings" is warehouse vocabulary and should not surface.

## Facts established while designing this — do not re-derive

- **The points column is safe.** The synthetic 3-1-0 tally lives in `int_team_season_record`. This
  table reads `mart_standings` ← `fct_standings` ← `base_apif__standings` ←
  `stg_apif__standings.sql:35`, which is `json_value(team_row, '$.points')` — the **provider's**
  points. The cups-points defect does not reach this page. All twelve active competitions are
  domestic leagues in any case.
- **The page renders no `metric_catalogue` metric at all**, by construction. The table's column
  headers are page chrome: the catalogue has no `played`/`wins`/`draws`/`losses`/`goal_difference`
  row, and its one `points_won` (team) row is the synthetic tally — a different number. So the
  "never type a metric label, always look it up" rule has nothing to bind to here. Do not add a
  catalogue lookup to satisfy it.
- **No goals-for/against column is possible** — `mart_standings` carries `goals_diff` only.
- **No promotion/relegation shading** — the registry carries no zone rules and we do not invent
  them.
- **Round names are provider strings.** The mart stores `"Regular Season - 25"`; rendering
  "Matchday 25" means parsing it before it can be localised. Uncosted i18n work.
- **The export already produces this payload.** `shape_competition_payload` in
  `scripts/export_site_data.py:600` emits standings + top scorers + fixtures per
  competition-season. ⚠ It is not yet written into `site_v2/src/data/` — wiring it is part of this
  build. **Zero new marts.**

## Top scorers — CUT, deliberately

A 7-row goals board was in the first draft and was removed.

Leaderboards are not homeless: `site_architecture.md:48` reserves
`/{competition-slug}/top-scorers/` and `content_architecture.md:122` has a Scorers tab. So a board
on the hub was a teaser for a page that does not exist — the browse-chip 404 one layer up. It also
picked one of the nine boards `mart_leaderboards` already produces per competition-season, with no
ruling behind the pick.

⚠ `mart_leaderboards` ranks `partition by league_code, season_api_year` — **per-league is its
native grain**, so the top-scorers page needs no new warehouse work. The pooling problem is
specific to the home page's boards (#40/#41).

## The page spec it must declare

```
entity:            competition
canonical:         self
hreflang:          all-locales
schema_org:        SportsOrganization      (least-certain field; ItemList is the alternative)
links:             inbound_hub "home"  →  outbound ["team", "fixture"]
page_count_driver: count(active competitions with a current-season standings row) × count(locales)
url_permanence:    permanent
```

⚠ **No `player` outbound edge** — player pages do not exist and declaring one would overstate.

⚠ **`inbound_hub: "home"` is FALSE until the browse chips become anchors.** So **this MR must
carry #44's tag swap**, or the hub ships as an orphan itself. `system.css` already scopes the
hover affordance to `a.linkchip`, so the tag swap is the whole edit.

## Open

- **Season archives and a switcher — recommended OUT of v1.** ~12 competitions × ~10 seasons × 3
  locales ≈ 360 pages of bare table, against a minimum-data gate (#845) that is not built.
- **The four planned sub-pages** (`/table/`, `/fixtures/`, `/top-scorers/`, `/{season}/`) are
  untouched by #46: the hub's two blocks are stacked and visible, not hidden behind a control.
  Whether the sub-pages carry the *full* versions while the hub carries compact ones is the next
  design question.
- `schema_org` — `SportsOrganization` proposed, not verified against a rich-result requirement.

defects) live outside the repo in the design-mocks folder beside the home-page work:
`gen_competition_hub.py` · `check_competition_hub.py` · `competition_hub_mock.html`.

### #54 Competitions page /{locale}/competitions/ - build it, and record the 2026-08-10 design (grouped by display_group, not confederation)

_opened · created 2026-08-11_

Build `/{locale}/competitions/` — the page the site menu's **first** item points at.

**Designed and CPO-reviewed 2026-08-10.** Build from here.

⚠ **Not the competition page.** That is `/{locale}/{slug}/` — one league — and it is **#47**. This
is the index above it. The two were conflated in review; the plural/singular distinction is worth
keeping in writing.

## Why

`SiteHeader.astro`'s first nav item is **Competitions** and it leads nowhere — an inert `<span>`,
because this page has never existed (#48). It is also the only one of the four empty menu items
with a route already reserved in `site_architecture.md` §3.

## What it shows

Every competition we carry: **logo · name · country · tier**, each row linking to that
competition's own page.

**What earns it a page rather than being another chip row:** the home page's browse block is one
flat row of chips (#44) — a name and nothing else. This carries the country, the tier and a
grouping. If it were another chip row it should not exist.

## ⭐ The grouping — and the mistake worth recording

The first version grouped by **confederation**, with headings *Europe / North & Central America /
Asia*. That was wrong in a way that was not obvious, and the CPO caught it by asking where the
grouping came from:

- the **values** were real — `confederation` is a registry field the export already carries;
- the **labels** were typed into the mock. **No source for them exists anywhere in the repo**;
- the **axis itself was invented**. `site_architecture.md` §4 documents exactly two browse axes,
  `display_group` and country. Country is ruled out (#45), and confederation is neither.

**It now groups by `display_group`**, which is genuinely part of the data model:

- it comes from a **seed** — `dbt_project/seeds/competition_types.csv`, `competition_type →
  display_group`;
- its labels **already exist in all three locales** — `groupLeagues`, `groupCups`,
  `groupContinentalClub`, `groupNationalTeams` in `strings.ts`. Nothing is typed;
- it is the axis the home page's browse block already uses.

⚠ **Today it yields ONE group.** All twelve active competitions are `domestic_league`. A heading
over the entire list carries no information, so the page renders **no headings while there is one
group**, and grows them by itself when a cup or a continental competition is onboarded. Order is
the registry's `sort_order`.

⚠ **A blank `display_group` means "not browsable", and the seed uses it deliberately** —
`club_friendly_domestic`, `club_friendly_international`, `national_team_friendly`. Those are
EXCLUDED from this page rather than given a heading. Found because the guard fired on a blank
value: the seed was right and the guard was too strict.

## Everything on the page is read, not typed

The set, the order, the grouping, the country, the tier and the slug all come from
`docs/competition_registry.yml` and `competition_types.csv` at render time. **Onboarding a
competition adds a row here with no edit** — the zero-file rule applied to a page.

Two values are still typed in the mock and both are guarded:

- **the display NAME** — no readable source exists. This is its own issue (see Related).
- **the timezone** — `kickoff_timezone` is the provider's request zone, not the venue's.

## Interaction

Each row is a **row target** per the interaction standard (#52): the row is the link, it lifts on
hover, the chevron is the at-rest affordance, nothing underlines. Row grammar deliberately mirrors
the competition heading in the matches block — logo, name, chevron — so the two pages read as one
system.

## The page spec it must declare

```
entity:            competition        (an index of them — see the open question below)
canonical:         self
hreflang:          all-locales
schema_org:        ItemList
links:             inbound_hub "home"  →  outbound ["competition"]
page_count_driver: count(locales)      — ONE page per locale, not per competition
url_permanence:    permanent
```

⚠ `inbound_hub: "home"` is only true once the **menu items become links**. Same trap as the browse
chips and the competition hub: a page whose only inbound route is an inert `<span>` is an orphan
on arrival. **This MR must make the Competitions nav item an anchor** — `system.css` styles
`.mainnav a` and `.mainnav span` identically, so the tag swap is the whole edit.

⚠ `entity` may need a new value in `page-spec.schema.json` — its enum is
`team | player | fixture | competition | home`, and an INDEX of competitions is not a competition.
