### #55 Competition display name has no single source: registry and dim_league disagree, and neither is the name we show

_opened · created 2026-08-11_

**CPO, 2026-08-10:** *"We need the displayed names in the data somewhere, one single source of
truth so it consistently shows the same name used everywhere we use it."*

A competition's displayed name has **no single source today**. It has two, they disagree, and
neither is the name we want to show.

## The three names, and where each comes from

| Source | Value for BL1 | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/competition_registry.yml` → `name` | `1. Fußball-Bundesliga` | `export_site_data.py:609` (competition payload), `:915` (nav), `:960` (landing/browse) |
| `core.dim_league.league_name` | the provider's, **unverified** — needs the warehouse | `export_site_data.py:821` (fixture payload) |
| what the CPO says it is | **`Bundesliga`** | nothing |

So **the fixture page and the browse chips can already print different names for the same
league**, and the one the registry supplies is the legal form the CPO rejected: *"1.
Fussball-Bundesliga is just Bundesliga"*.

⚠ The committed `site_v2/src/data/competitions.json` carries the registry form, so this is live,
not theoretical.

## What is needed

**One field, in the warehouse, that every surface reads.** Published by `dim_league`, with
corrections applied in `base_apif__league_entity` — exactly the ruling already made for TEAM names
(#851: *base prepares the override, the core dim publishes; never coalesce in the dim*).

The registry keeps what it is good at — `slug`, `tier`, `confederation`, `sort_order`,
`competition_type`, `country`, `history_seasons` — and **stops carrying a display name**.

⚠ **The provider's name is not automatically right either.** It is very likely "Bundesliga" (good)
but also "Major League Soccer" (which the CPO flagged as too long for a chip in #44). So a
correction layer is needed regardless of which raw source wins — which is precisely why this
mirrors the team-name work rather than being a one-line change.

## One name, not two

The CPO asked for *the same name used everywhere*. So: **one display name per competition**, used
on the chip, the heading, the H1, the group head, the breadcrumb and the title. Not a short form
plus a long form.

⚠ This retires the open `label_short` style question for competitions before it is asked. If a
constrained surface ever cannot fit the one name, that is a layout problem to solve there, not a
second name to maintain.

## Scope check — is it only competitions?

**No, and that is the reason to do it properly.** The same shape already bit team names and has
already been ruled on:

| Entity | Name source today | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Team | `dim_team`, a passive pass-through of the provider | #850/#851 — 14 verified corrections, base prepares / dim publishes |
| **Competition** | **registry AND `dim_league`, disagreeing** | **this issue** |
| Player | provider, via `dim_player` | slug carries the id; name unreviewed |
| Coach, country | not ingested / ruled out | — |

So this is the competition instance of a pattern the repo already has a ruling for. Follow it
rather than inventing a second mechanism.

## First tasks

1. **Read what `dim_league.league_name` actually contains** for all twelve active competitions.
   Everything above treats it as unverified because there is no warehouse access right now.
2. Decide the display name for each of the twelve, against an external source of record — the
   same discipline as #850, which found 14 wrong team names that way.
3. Apply corrections in `base_apif__league_entity`; publish from `dim_league`.
4. Point **every** export path at it — `export_site_data.py` lines 609, 821, 915, 960 — and delete
   `name` from the registry so there is nothing to drift back to.
5. Add a guard: no consumption-layer file may read a competition name from the registry.

## Blocked work

The four page designs all render a competition name and all use a **typed stand-in** today
(`SHORT_NAME` in the mocks, guarded so it cannot drift from the registry's set, but still typed):

- **#54** competitions page · **#47** competition page · **#50** the Next-matches block (its
  group head is a competition name) · the home page's browse row (#44)

None of them can ship an honest name until this lands.

⚠ Do not touch `!27`.

### #56 i18n: the continental-club browse group is labelled "European club" in all three locales, but 5 of its 9 members are not European

_opened · created 2026-08-11_

The `continental-club` browse group is labelled **"European club"** in all three locales. Five of
its nine members are not European.

## The defect

`site_v2/src/i18n/strings.ts`:

```
:200  groupContinentalClub: "European club"          (en)
:352  groupContinentalClub: "Europapokal"            (de)
:515  groupContinentalClub: "Euroopan seurakilpailut" (fi)
```

The German and Finnish are, if anything, more specific than the English — *Europapokal* and
*Euroopan seurakilpailut* both name Europe outright.

## What is actually in that group

`display_group = continental-club` comes from `dbt_project/seeds/competition_types.csv`, which
maps `continental_club` and `continental_super_cup` to it. The registry currently has **nine**
competitions of those types:

| | league_code | Competition | Region |
|---|---|---|---|
| ✓ | UCL | UEFA Champions League | Europe |
| ✓ | UEL | UEFA Europa League | Europe |
| ✓ | UECL | UEFA Europa Conference League | Europe |
| ✓ | UESC | UEFA Super Cup | Europe |
| ✗ | **LIBER** | **Copa Libertadores** | South America |
| ✗ | **CAFCL** | **CAF Champions League** | Africa |
| ✗ | **AFCCL** | **AFC Champions League Elite** | Asia |
| ✗ | **CCCU** | **CONCACAF Champions Cup** | North/Central America |
| ✗ | **CWC** | **FIFA Club World Cup** | International |

So the label is wrong for **five of nine**, and wrong for the one with the widest scope of all —
the Club World Cup.

## Why it has not bitten yet

All nine are `status: in_progress`; only the twelve `domestic_league` competitions are active. The
browse block (`home/BrowseGrid.astro`) therefore renders a single group today and never reaches
this key. **It becomes visible the moment any continental competition is onboarded**, and it will
be visible on the home page — the most exposed surface there is.

⚠ Found while designing the competitions page (**#54**), which groups by the same
`display_group`. Its preview across all 45 registry competitions is what made it obvious.

## Fix

The label should describe the CATEGORY, not a continent — the group is *club competitions between
clubs of different countries*. Candidates:

- **"Continental club"** — matches the `display_group` value itself, and is what `content_architecture.md` §4 calls it
- "International club"
- "Club competitions"

⚠ **The label is a CPO naming call**, not an engineering one — and it needs DE and FI, where the
current strings are the most wrong.

⚠ **Do not just fix English.** All three locales name Europe explicitly.

## Also worth checking while in there

The sibling keys carry the same risk of assuming a region or a scope:
`groupLeagues` ("Leagues"), `groupCups` ("Cups"), `groupNationalTeams` ("National teams"). Those
three read as scope-neutral, but they have never been reviewed against the full 45-competition
registry either — only against the twelve active leagues.

⚠ Do not touch `!27`.

### #57 Group competitions by competition_type, not display_group - and two competitions the taxonomy cannot classify (Club World Cup, Intercontinental Cup)

_opened · created 2026-08-11_

**CPO ruling, 2026-08-10:** the competitions page groups by **`competition_type`** — the taxonomy
itself — not by `display_group`, which is a rollup of it.

## The three levels, and why the coarsest was the wrong choice

All three already live in the data model, keyed by each registry entry's `competition_type`:

| Level | Values | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `competition_type` | 12 | `docs/competition_registry.yml` → `seeds/competition_registry.csv` |
| `entity_type` | 2 — club / national | `seeds/competition_types.csv` |
| `display_group` | 4 — a **rollup** for browsing | `seeds/competition_types.csv` |

The competitions page (#54) was grouped by `display_group` because it is the only level with i18n
labels. The cost of that rollup, on the real 45-competition registry:

- **World Cup, Euros, Nations League and qualifiers all in one bucket** ("National teams", 15)
- **Champions League in the same bucket as the Club World Cup** ("European club", 9)

## What ships instead — 7 groups

| Group | n |
|---|---|
| Domestic leagues | 16 |
| Continental club | 8 |
| Continental championships | 7 |
| Qualifiers | 7 |
| Domestic cups | 5 |
| World Cup | 1 |
| Continental super cup | 1 |

Two single-member groups today; both grow. **It also dissolves #56** — there is no "European
club" bucket left to be wrong about, so that issue is resolved by this change rather than by a
rename.

⚠ **Cost: new i18n keys in three locales.** Only the four `display_group` labels exist today
(`groupLeagues`, `groupCups`, `groupContinentalClub`, `groupNationalTeams`). The English group
names above are a **proposal**, not approved copy, and DE/FI do not exist at all.

## ⛔ Two competitions the taxonomy cannot classify correctly

**1. FIFA Club World Cup (`CWC`) is typed `continental_club`.** It is global, not continental.
Under the new grouping it would sit under "Continental club" beside the Europa League, which is
wrong on the page and wrong in the warehouse — 9 dbt models join `competition_types.csv` and would
inherit the misclassification.

**2. FIFA Intercontinental Cup is not in the registry at all.**

Both need a `competition_type` that does not exist yet — something like `intercontinental_club`,
`entity_type: club`. ⚠ The exact value and its label are a **CPO naming call**.

⚠ `WCQIP` ("WC Qualification Intercontinental Playoffs") is a **different competition** — a
national-team qualifier, correctly typed `qualifying`. Do not conflate the two on the word
"intercontinental".

## The fix is a seed edit, not a new model

⚠ **No new dim is needed.** The taxonomy is already seated in the data model and dbt already
consumes it:

- `seeds/competition_registry.csv` — joined by **13** models
- `seeds/competition_types.csv` — joined by **9** models
- `scripts/check_competition_type_seed.py` already **fails CI** if the registry uses a
  `competition_type` with no seed row

So adding the type means: one row in `competition_types.csv`, re-type `CWC` in the registry, add
the Intercontinental Cup entry, run `scripts/sync_dbt_vars.py`. The existing guard then keeps the
registry and the seed in step by itself.

**What is genuinely absent is exposure via a core dim.** `dim_league` carries provider identity
only — `league_name`, `league_type`, `league_country`, `league_logo_url`, `country_flag_url` — and
no competition_type, so every consumer joins a seed directly. That is the same seeds-as-
configuration pattern the metric catalogue uses, so it is a legitimate choice rather than a
defect. Surfacing it on a dim is **optional and not a prerequisite** for this change.

## Order of work

1. Decide the new `competition_type` value and its label (CPO).
2. Seed + registry edits, `sync_dbt_vars.py`, CI guard confirms.
3. i18n keys for the seven group labels, three locales.
4. Repoint the competitions page (#54) from `display_group` to `competition_type`.
5. Close **#56** — the bucket it describes no longer exists.

## Related

- **#54** the competitions page · **#56** the "European club" mislabel, resolved by this
- **#55** the display-name single source — same class of problem, different field
- ⚠ Do not touch `!27`.

### #62 Every page block is populated from ONE mart - the competitions page would read four sources, because the registry seed is projected down to three columns

_opened · created 2026-08-11_

**CPO, 2026-08-11:** *"if we allow this now some file here, warehouse there, some other file here
etc. … We need a consistent approach on how the contents of the website of any page are
populated."*

Correct, and the repo already carries the rule — it is just not true in practice.

**`docs/content_architecture.md` §1:** *"One block = one mart, parameterised by `league_code` /
season / entity … Nothing computes in a page — pages only arrange blocks."*

## What the competitions page (#54) would actually read today

Designing that page surfaced the violation. To render one row it needs **four sources**:

| what | from |
|---|---|
| the set, order, country, confederation, slug | `docs/competition_registry.yml` — read as a **YAML file** by the export |
| the category and its label | `dbt_project/seeds/competition_types.csv` — read as a **CSV file** with `open()` |
| the region label | `confederations.csv` — a new seed, would be read the same way (#57) |
| the display name and the logo | `core.dim_league` — the **warehouse** (#55) |

Four sources, no rule about which owns what, and the page's provenance table becomes a story
rather than a column reference. That is unmaintainable and it is not what §1 says.

## Why it ended up like this — the registry seed is projected down to three columns

The registry **is** in the warehouse. `scripts/sync_dbt_vars.py` generates
`dbt_project/seeds/competition_registry.csv` from the YAML, and 13 models join it.

But it carries **three columns**:

```
league_code,competition_type,parent_competition
```

`country`, `confederation`, `slug`, `sort_order`, `tier` and `season_type` never reach the
warehouse. So anything needing them has no choice but to read the YAML directly — which is exactly
what `export_site_data.py` does (`_registry_competitions()`, `:911`). The workaround is old enough
to look like a design.

⚠ **This is already half-diagnosed.** `docs/wireframes/99_gaps_register.md` **GAP-28** proposes
precisely this — *"Project `tier` and `season_type` from the YAML registry into the seed via
`scripts/sync_dbt_vars.py`"* — **design approved by the CPO 2026-08-08, build not started.** It
asked for two columns because that was what the home page's league pools needed. The general
problem is the same and needs four more.

## The rule

**Every page block is populated from exactly one mart. The export selects and renames; it never
derives, and it never reads a config file to fill in what the mart lacks.**

```
registry.yml  ──sync_dbt_vars──>  competition_registry.csv  ─┐
competition_types.csv  ──────────────────────────────────────┼──>  mart_competition_index
confederations.csv  ─────────────────────────────────────────┤          (one row per competition)
core.dim_league  (name, logo)  ───────────────────────────────┘                │
                                                                               v
                                              export_site_data.py  ->  one JSON  ->  the page
```

The seeds stay the authoring surface — that does not change, and neither does the zero-file rule:
onboarding a competition is still one registry row, `sync_dbt_vars.py` regenerates the seed, dbt
rebuilds the mart, the export dumps it.

What changes is that **the website never reads an authoring surface directly.**

## Order of work

1. `sync_dbt_vars.py` projects the display fields into `competition_registry.csv` —
   `country`, `confederation`, `slug`, `sort_order`, plus GAP-28's `tier` and `season_type`.
   ⚠ `scripts/check_registry_var_sync.py` already fails CI when the seed drifts from the registry;
   it checks `league_code → (competition_type, parent_competition)` and must be extended to the
   new columns, or the guard silently stops covering most of the file.
2. `competition_types.csv` gains its new columns and `confederations.csv` lands as a seed (#57).
3. Build `mart_competition_index` — one row per competition, every column the page renders.
4. Repoint `export_site_data.py` at the mart. Delete the YAML read and the `open()` on the seed
   CSV for this page.
5. The page spec declares **one** source.

## ⚠ This supersedes an earlier ruling, and that should be explicit

`page-spec.schema.json` documents a CPO ruling of **2026-08-03** that generalised the spec's
`mart` field to accept `registry:` and `seed:` types, *"because the home page's browse block reads
the competition registry, which the zero-file rule deliberately keeps out of the model layer"*.

That premise is wrong: the registry is **already** in the model layer as a seed — just with three
columns. So the generalisation solved the symptom. Under this issue the `registry:` and `seed:`
source types become the exception rather than the pattern, and the schema's documentation of that
ruling needs rewriting rather than leaving both versions standing.

## Scope — not just this page

Every surface that reads an authoring file directly:

- the **home page's browse block** (`registry:competition_registry` in `index.spec.json`)
- `nav.json` and the committed `site_v2/src/data/competitions.json`, both registry-only
- the competitions page (#54) and the competition page (#47) as they are designed

## Cost, stated rather than discovered

The competitions page currently builds with **no BigQuery at all** — `fetch_nav()`'s docstring says
so. Under this rule it gains a warehouse dependency. It was going to gain one anyway for the name
(#55) and the logo, so the question is not whether but when.

## Related

- **#55** the display name single source — the first field that forced this question
- **#57** the taxonomy seed reshape · **#54** the page that surfaced it · **#58** per-element
  provenance, which is only checkable once "one element ← one mart column" is true
- **GAP-28** in `docs/wireframes/99_gaps_register.md` — the same fix, approved, unbuilt

⚠ Do not touch `!27`.

### #105 Competition display label: compose name + season in the warehouse

_opened · created 2026-09-05_

A competition entity carries its NAME only (league_name_overrides seed, applied in base_apif__leagues). A season is not part of the name: the competition is "FIFA World Cup" and 2026 is the season, and the registry slug (world-cup) already follows that rule.

But an active season-scoped surface should read "FIFA World Cup 2026", not "FIFA World Cup". That composition is warehouse logic and does not exist yet.

Needed: a season-aware display label on the mart that serves competition-scoped pages, so the frontend selects a served string and composes nothing. Applies beyond the World Cup: any competition shown in a season context.

Context: CPO 2026-09-04, "World Cup is the competition, 2026 is the season, yes, but when it is active we show world cup 2026 and not just world cup. the logic is defined in the warehouse."

### #128 Competitions hub: recheck and approve the design, data sources and links

_opened · created 2026-09-12_

**Requested by:** Rami

## What exactly

- [x] A review of **Competitions hub**, for the CPO to approve on this issue before anything is built or rebuilt:
  1. what is on the page, block by block, in plain words;
  2. where each block's data comes from — a warehouse model, or a named gap where nothing serves it yet;
  3. which hub reaches the page, and what the page links on to.
- [x] The approved design is recorded here, in this issue, and the design chain (`docs/wireframes/00_overview.md`) points at it. Nothing about the page is settled anywhere else.
- [x] Build issues are filed against this one only once the design is approved.

**State today:** built (filters and the competition list); rows are not clickable because the competition page does not exist.

## Why

The roadmap is the site's menu, in order, each hub before the pages behind it, and every page rechecked by the CPO — built or not — because the earlier agreements may be stale and a built page is not a proof it can be built to the current design. One issue per page is the single place where its design, its data sources and its links are agreed.

## How

1. Put the current state in front of the CPO: the built page in the browser, or the wireframe rendered, with the data source beside every block.
2. He approves, changes or strikes, one page at a time.
3. Record the outcome here; correct or retire whatever document disagrees with it in the same MR that builds it.

---

## The approved design (CPO rulings, 2026-09-14)

Consolidated from the review notes below this description. Where a note and this section disagree, this section is current.

### The page

`/{lang}/competitions/`, behind the Competitions menu item. Breadcrumb "Home › Competitions", heading "Competitions", then the filters and the list.

### Filters

- **Kept as built:** two rows, both single-choice and combining — Clubs / National teams, and region (Europe, South America, North & Central America, Africa, Asia, Oceania, World). Filtering on the page, no reload; a group with no row left disappears.
- **Defect to fix in the build:** the script that hides an empty group decides by on-screen visibility (`offsetParent`), so a page loaded in a tab that is not displayed hides every group until a filter is touched (seen live 2026-09-14). Hide a group from the filter state instead.

### The list

- **Groups: one per competition kind**, the kind from the competition-type seed, the heading its translated label. Eight today: Domestic leagues, Domestic cups, Continental club cups, Continental super cups, Club World Cup, Continental championships, National team qualifiers, World Cup. A new kind gets its group automatically.
- **Translations:** the six kinds with no competition yet (domestic super cups, continental club qualifiers, Intercontinental Cup, the three friendlies) get German and Finnish labels; a guard checks every kind in the seed has all three languages, not only the kinds on the page.
- **Group order: the shared key** (has an upcoming fixture, then day, region rank, kickoff, code), each group placed by its earliest-sorting member, so the order moves with the calendar. No fixed order.
- **Row order inside a group:** the same key; competitions with nothing upcoming last, most recently played first.
- **Row content:** crest, name, and a place — the country for leagues and domestic cups, the region for everything else. Nothing else on the row.
- **The country in the reader's language:** regions are translated today, the 18 countries are English on every page. **#69** (the country table) is the build item, on the existing pattern: English name + key in the warehouse, DE/FI in the site's one translation file, the copy gate covering the keys.
- **Which competitions: all of them** — every competition the warehouse covers (48, all with ingestion on), in season or between seasons.

### Data

`marts.mart_competition_index`, read whole: name, crest, kind and its label key, region label key or country, region rank, next and last kickoff. Group and region names via the seed keys; country names via #69.

### Links

- **Out: a row links to that competition's page** (`/{lang}/{competition}/`, #129). Today the rows are not links.
- **In:** the header menu item; the breadcrumb on every competition page; the footer item goes live per the Home menu ruling (#127).

### Rulings that landed elsewhere

- **#57:** the `display_group` column of the competition-type seed is deleted; a competition we ingest is one we show (an onboarded friendly kind appears in its own group). Displayed names unaffected.
- **#69:** the country table, first consumer this page.

### Documents this supersedes

`docs/wireframes/08_browse.md` (the competitions index spec; still describes country pages `/football/{country}/` that are not in the menu and not built — to be struck or moved) — corrected in the MR that builds against this issue.

### Build items

Filed against this issue once ticked: row links; the empty-group fix; the six kinds' DE/FI labels plus the guard; the wireframe correction. Owned elsewhere: #57, #69.

### #129 Competition page (Bundesliga, Premier League, …): design, data sources and links

_opened · created 2026-09-12_

**Requested by:** Rami

## What exactly

- [x] A review of **Competition page (Bundesliga, Premier League, …)**, for the CPO to approve on this issue before anything is built or rebuilt:
  1. what is on the page, block by block, in plain words;
  2. where each block's data comes from — a warehouse model, or a named gap where nothing serves it yet;
  3. which hub reaches the page, and what the page links on to.
- [x] The approved design is recorded here, in this issue, and the design chain (`docs/wireframes/00_overview.md`) points at it. Nothing about the page is settled anywhere else.
- [x] Build issues are filed against this one only once the design is approved.

**State today (2026-09-16): the page is fully approved** — three tabs. The Overview is built (#149) and reworked below (its corrections ride on #151); the Matchdays tab is approved (#150 builds it); the Rankings tab is approved (#151 builds it, on #152's metric groups).

## The approved design — the competition page

The page is **three tabs, each a standalone page with an identical header and tab bar: Overview · Matchdays · Rankings** (for a cup or tournament the second reads **Rounds**, driven by the phase key). The tab labels in the three languages: Overview / Übersicht / Yleiskatsaus · Matchdays / Spieltage / Kierrokset (Rounds / Runden / Kierrokset) · Rankings / Rankings / Rankingit (DE "Rankings" ruled 2026-09-17). Ruled 2026-09-16, superseding the four tabs of 2026-09-15 and the labels tried on the way (Teams / Players, Team stats, Team rankings / Player rankings — measured too long for four tabs at 375px in three languages). **The header never changes with the tab** (crest · name · meta line), and there is **no page title under the tab bar** (rendered, rejected: "looks like we had no idea what to do"); the browser title carries the page's long name for search. The **tab bar fits its tabs in one row at 375px in all three languages, no sideways scrolling** — the tabs share the row, the side padding is what the label needs; a measured test in the build (the built Overview fails it today). Unbuilt tabs are inert labels until built; each tab's address is the builder's, optimised for search.

**Rules that bind every block on every tab:**
- a block is a **shared component fed by the same mart wherever it appears** (the table row, the fixture row, the fact row, the board are the site's rows);
- **one distance from a block name to its first line: the heading's 14px**, nothing added by the content (a date heading or a fact row opening a block carries no space of its own); measured 14 / 14 / 49 / 23 before, 14 everywhere after;
- **block names (the section heading) are 13px** capitals, from 11px ("it somewhat gets buried");
- **the number a block is ordered by is bold, 15px, the accent colour, everywhere** — the standings' Pts is the reference; no per-block colour;
- **a row that leads somewhere is one link, the whole row, lit on hover; within one block every row is a link or none is**; an underline is for a word inside text; a heading that leads somewhere carries a chevron at rest, never an underline;
- **every content block has a name**, and a block with nothing to show is absent;
- the export selects and renders, never computes; every displayed value is a mart column.

### Overview tab — approved (CPO, 2026-09-15, reworked 2026-09-16)

Top to bottom: **header · sentence · tab bar · Table · Deserved points table · The season in numbers.** Nothing else. Struck on the way: "In form", "Top scorers", a "Table" tab, a "Scorers" tab, an "Every matchday" link, **Next matches** (2026-09-16: "redundant, we have it on the next tab" — the Matchdays tab opens on it; Home keeps its block), the Better / Worse boards, "The match that matters next" as a fact row.

**Header.** Crest · competition name · meta line **Country · Season 2026/27 · Matchday 4**, all three from one row of `mart_competition_index` (region key exists; season label #105; round phase key + number #148), the words translated as site copy. Tier struck. Under it **one data-backed template sentence** ("{leader} lead after {played} matches, {gap} points clear of {second}"), generated by #145; cups and group stages get their own template or none. The sentence is the Overview's only; no other tab carries one.

**Block 1 — Table.** Columns `#` · crest · club · P · W · D · L · **Goals** (scored:conceded, `10:1`) · GD · Pts; striped rows, **no line under a row — the head rule is a table's only line** (ruled 2026-09-17, on #153; the Overview render of 2026-09-16 still shows row lines); points bold in the accent colour; **the whole row is the link** to the team page. Narrow screens hide W · D · L · Goals; the heading and the rows share one fixed column list so they cannot drift. No movement arrows (no standings history), no champion/cup/promoted letters (not held).
*Source rule:* every column is **the provider's official standings row as published** (`fct_standings` → `mart_standings`), nothing computed — a fact from the source, like a match score, and a defensible deviation from "every displayed number is a catalogued metric". Goals for/against are in the payload (`$.all.goals.for/against`) and must be extracted there, never summed from fixtures. The rule "facts taken from the provider as published versus metrics the warehouse computes, never mixed inside one block" is in `docs/metric_layer.md`. #147 reconciles the provider's points with the 3-1-0 tally.
*Groups and cups:* one table per group under the group's name (groups, conferences, split-season rounds); the provider's cross-group ranking tables are dropped; `mart_standings` carries the table kind as a column and the page filters on it. **The league-phase or group tables stay on the page through the knockout rounds**; cups with no table phase show the header and The season in numbers only. No bracket, no past results.

**Block 2 — Deserved points table** (DE "Tabelle nach verdienten Punkten", FI "Ansaittujen pisteiden taulukko"). The section heading, then one explanation: *"Deserved points are the points a team's shot balance usually earns. Shot balance is shots on goal created minus shots on goal conceded. Teams with fewer points than deserved are better than the table says; teams with more are worse."* Then **every team of the competition-season in one table ranked by deserved points, highest first:** `#` (the deserved rank) · crest · club · **Balance** (the shot balance: shots on goal for minus against per match, signed) · **Deserved** (bold accent, the ordering number) · Pts · **Diff** (actual minus deserved — the catalogue's `deserved_points_gap`, signed; Mainz −2.7). The table row, the whole row to the team page, one fixed track list. Rejected on the way: the two three-row boards (Better / Worse than the table says); a shots-on-goal for:against column; table order with deserved beside it. Source `mart_team_profile` (`deserved_points`, `points`, `deserved_points_gap`, `shots_on_goal_difference_per_match`). Domestic leagues only, pooled per league-season; cups and tournaments have no block. Open on the model, not the block: values exist for the current season only, and a three-matchday fit is thin.

**Block 3 — The season in numbers.** Six **fact rows**, in this order: Goals per match (one decimal; context "104 goals in 27 matches") · Home wins ("14 of 27"; "5 draws, 8 away wins") · Biggest margin (the score, home–away, in the locale's format; context the match and matchday) · Most goals in a match (same shape, no goal count) · Longest unbeaten run ("3 matches"; the teams sharing it) · Longest winless run. "vs" between teams, a copy key per locale. Ties: a tie on the biggest margin goes to the match with more goals, on the most goals to the bigger margin, then the earlier kickoff. **Every row links to the leaderboard behind its number** (the CPO's direction, 2026-09-16): matches ranked by margin / by goals (a match leaderboard, a new page type), teams ranked by their run, and the lists behind the two league-wide numbers — six pages under Leaderboards, filed as requirements on **#140**, the rows inert until each exists. Source: `mart_competition_season_summary` (one row per competition-season; streaks from `mart_team_profile`). The match-that-matters flag (`is_match_that_matters` on `mart_next_matchday`, lowest sum of table positions on the next matchday, ties to the earlier kickoff) stays in the warehouse and is displayed on the Matchdays tab.

**The fact row — a block type** (team page, player page, match page head-to-head): label (ink, regular) · value (ink, semi-bold: a number, a score or a match) · context (muted, under the value). Wide: label left, value and context right-aligned; narrow (under ~420px): stacked left-aligned. The whole row links to the thing behind the value. **A name, a "Matchday N" and a date never break inside themselves.** Home for the definition: the design chain's block standard, next to the fixture row and the table row.

*After the season:* the page keeps everything for the latest season with data; the meta line's round part reads the last round played (#148).

### Matchdays tab — approved (CPO, 2026-09-16)

Address `/{locale}/{competition-slug}/fixtures/` for every kind of competition (the builder's, optimised for search: fans type "fixtures" / "Spielplan", never "matchdays"; the tab label stays Matchdays, Rounds for a cup); the browser title per language names fixtures and results with the season; the breadcrumb Home › Competitions › {competition} › {tab}, the competition a link to the Overview. Header and tab bar identical to the Overview's. **No sentence on this tab.**

**One content block: "Schedule"** (DE Spielplan, FI Otteluohjelma), and no second — brainstormed and dropped: The match that matters (the row repeated), Lucky and unlucky (one row on matchday 3, often none), Form going in, Who is on a run, The matchday in numbers. Under the tab bar, first the **picker** on its own full-width line — **‹ MATCHDAY N ›** with a **Next** tag on the next matchday, the arrows pinned to the two edges and the title centred so nothing shifts between matchdays, stepping to the neighbouring matchday — then the block below it with its name as a section heading, in the Overview's section structure and the site's stylesheet with no spacing of its own. One matchday on screen at a time; the tab opens on the next matchday. No script (the radio + CSS mechanism the site's tabs already use). Under it the date heading per day and the site's match row: a played row is that row plus the score (winner by weight, never hue); an unplayed row carries the kick-off in the venue's clock with the zone label (#146); a match with a date but no time yet shows **"TBC"** (a copy key per language) in the time slot; **the flagged match of the next matchday carries a "Top match" tag** (DE "Topspiel", FI "Huippuottelu") on its row before the kick-off, in the Next tag's style, the row otherwise unchanged. **Every row is a link, no exceptions:** a played match → the match stats page (#132 designs it); the next and every later match → the match preview page, the same page for every unplayed match of the season, showing both teams' form as of today with the date stated and one sentence built from the two forms (#132 / #145). Struck on the way: one long page of every matchday; a picker strip that scrolls sideways; a wrapped grid of 34 chips; the block name above the picker; the picker on the right of the heading line (the Next tag moved the arrows); no page for a match beyond the next matchday; a reduced page for far matches; "noindex" on later previews.

*Cups and tournaments:* the same block; the heading reads the round's name from the phase key (#148) — ‹ Round of 16 ›, ‹ Group stage · Matchday 2 › — the arrows step through the rounds in order; rounds not yet drawn do not exist, the picker stops at the last known one. *No next matchday:* after the season the tab opens on the last matchday played; before the first, on matchday 1.

*Source:* one new mart, every match of one competition-season, one row each, played and unplayed — round phase key + number, kick-off local + zone, status, score, both teams (name, crest, slug), the fixture slug, the next-matchday flag and the top-match flag. `mart_next_matchday` stays the thin read for Home; the Matches menu item (#131) reads the new mart by date.

### Rankings tab — approved (CPO, 2026-09-16)

Tab label **Rankings** (DE "Rankings", FI "Rankingit" proposed; on the build MR). Address the builder's, for search; no sentence; header and tab bar the Overview's. **No deserved points on this tab** — the idea lives on the Overview only. **The exhaustive lists live under the Leaderboards menu (#140)**; this tab is the competition's top rows.

**Two content blocks: "Team rankings" and "Player rankings"** (DE Team-Rankings / Spieler-Rankings, FI Tiimirankingit / Pelaajarankingit) — the only two names on the tab written by hand. Inside each block the boards sit under **metric groups**, whose key, order and names come from the catalogue and its copy (**#152**: the group `duels` becomes `one_on_one`, "One-on-one"); the group heading is the Matches page's level-1 group heading in size and air (17px bold, 34px above) **without its line** — ruled 2026-09-17, on #153: a metric group over boards carries no line; Home's competition group head over match rows keeps its 2px line (#50). A clear step over the 14px board names. Rejected on the way: a Teams | Players switch (hidden text reads as less important to search, one address anyway); prefixed block names; the Table block's smaller group heading (buried).

**Team boards, twelve, in the CPO's order:** Goals — goals per match · goals against per match (fewest first); Shooting — shots on goal per match · shots on goal against per match (fewest first) · shots on goal difference per match; Passing — passes per match · % pass accuracy; Defending — defensive actions per match; One-on-one — duels per match · % duels won; Discipline — yellow cards · red cards (season totals, most first). Dropped: clean sheets.

**Player boards, thirteen:** Goals — goals · assists; Shooting — shots on goal · % goals per shot on goal; Passing — passes · key passes · % pass accuracy; One-on-one — dribbles attempted · duels; Defending — defensive actions; Discipline — yellow cards · red cards (most first, as the teams'); Goalkeeping — saves. Dropped: goal contributions, % shots saved, dribbles completed, duels won. Player rows: rank · crest · name with the club under it · value; whole row to the player page. Rate boards keep the player leaderboard mart's rules (minutes ≥ 270, the position scope, 10 shots on goal for finishing); a board nobody qualifies for is absent (finishing, after three matchdays).

*Board rules:* rank · crest · name · value, the whole row to the team or player page; **five rows** by the tie-broken order the leaderboard marts carry (#114), the warehouse's dense rank shown as it is (equal values share a rank); values in the catalogue's format and precision (one decimal for rates, whole percents; two decimals rejected); a "fewest is best" board ranks ascending and says "fewest first" beside its name; **on a most-first board a value of 0 is not a ranking** — up to five rows above zero, fewer when fewer exist, the board absent when none; every board heading a chevron link to the full list (#140), inert until that page exists. Struck on the way: a "Top teams" wrapper block; underline-on-hover on a board name; three, then six rows; the full 18-row deserved table here; deserved boards here.

*Catalogue rulings:* **`clean_sheets` is a count and displays as a bare count everywhere** — its format changes from `count_fraction` to `integer`; `clean_sheets_pct` stays `percent`; the display contract's `3/5` and the fixture page's form window follow (#132 carries the pointer); **`points_won` keeps `points_fraction` ("13/15")**, a deliberate exception. **Two new team metrics**, `cards_yellow` and `cards_red` (season totals from the provider's team match statistics; id, label, definition, format `integer`, group `discipline`): their catalogue rows are put to the CPO on the build MR with the football-domain review, and their boards rank most first by ruling regardless of the direction the catalogue assigns; the player card boards rank most first the same way.

*Cups and tournaments:* the boards only; nations ranked the same way. *Source:* `mart_team_leaderboards` grows from four to the twelve team boards; `mart_leaderboards` (player) already ranks nine of the thirteen and adds dribbles attempted, duels, saves, and yellow / red cards as separate most-first boards; each list, its seed's accepted values and its singular test move together; pooled per league-season (2026-09-15).

## Build items

Filed already: **#105** season label · **#145** sentence generator · **#146** venue time zone · **#147** points reconciliation test · **#148** round phase key · **#69** country translation key · **#149** the Overview as first approved (merged) · **#150** the Matchdays tab · **#151** the Rankings tab, with the Overview's rework and the page-wide rules · **#152** the metric groups.

**#150 (Matchdays):** the competition-season fixtures mart · the tab page at `/fixtures/` with the picker and the Schedule block (the Top match tag included) · the block written into the design chain's block standard · the export reads the new mart per competition · the site build proven to carry every unplayed match page of every competition (a founding requirement, `docs/north_star.md` "Scale ambition") and a check that counts built match pages against the warehouse · the nightly warehouse read for every unplayed match measured and put to the CPO with the number · EN/DE/FI copy · the mock generator into `design-mocks/`.

**#151 (the Rankings tab + the Overview's rework + the page rules), on #152:** the team leaderboard mart's board set to twelve and the player mart's to thirteen, with their tests and accepted values · the two card metrics through the catalogue and the season rollup · `clean_sheets` to `integer` and every reader corrected · the Rankings page with its two blocks, the metric groups from #152 under the level-1 group heading, and the board component (five rows, zero rule, fewest-first note, chevron heading; the player row with the club under the name) · **the Overview reworked:** three-tab bar, Next matches removed, the Deserved points table in place of the two boards, the six fact rows as leaderboard links with the match-that-matters row removed · **the page-wide rules in `system.css` and the block standard:** the 14px heading gap, the 13px block name, the ordered-by number, the tab-bar fit test · `docs/site_architecture.md` gains the addresses · EN/DE/FI copy put to the CPO on the MR · the mock generators into `design-mocks/`.

## Why

The roadmap is the site's menu, in order, each hub before the pages behind it, and every page rechecked by the CPO — built or not — because the earlier agreements may be stale and a built page is not a proof it can be built to the current design. One issue per page is the single place where its design, its data sources and its links are agreed.

## How

1. Put the current state in front of the CPO: the built page in the browser, or the wireframe rendered, with the data source beside every block.
2. He approves, changes or strikes, one page at a time.
3. Record the outcome here; correct or retire whatever document disagrees with it in the same MR that builds it.

The rulings above are the consolidation of this issue's notes (2026-09-14, 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-16); a note and this text disagreeing is a defect in this text.

### #144 Competitions hub: build the approved design — row links, the hidden-groups fix, six missing labels, wireframe corrected

_closed · created 2026-09-14 · closed 2026-09-14_

**Requested by:** Rami

Builds the design approved on #128 (CPO, 2026-09-14). Only the parts this page owns; #57 (the dead `display_group` column) and #69 (the country table) are their own build items.

## What exactly

- [ ] Every row on `/{lang}/competitions/` is a link to that competition's page (`/{lang}/{competition}/`); 48 links on each language's page, none to a page that does not build.
- [ ] A page loaded in a background tab shows all eight groups when switched to: a group is hidden only when the checked filters leave it no row, decided from the filter state, never from on-screen visibility.
- [ ] Every competition kind in the seed has a German and a Finnish label, the six without one today included (domestic super cups, continental club qualifiers, Intercontinental Cup, domestic club friendlies, international club friendlies, national team friendlies); a build gate fails when any kind in the seed lacks a language.
- [ ] `docs/wireframes/08_browse.md` describes the page as approved on #128 and names #128 as the authority; the country-hub pages it still describes are struck; `docs/wireframes/00_overview.md` points at #128 for the competitions index.

## Why

The CPO approved the Competitions hub on #128; the built page has no row links, a script that can hide the whole list, six untranslatable kinds and a wireframe that still describes pages that do not exist.

## How

1. `CompetitionIndexGrid.astro`: the row becomes an `<a>` to `localeHref(lang, slug + "/")`; `slug` is already on every `mart_competition_index` row.
2. The empty-group collapse reads the two checked radios and each row's `data-entity-type` / `data-confederation`, and hides a group when no row matches; no `offsetParent`.
3. `strings.ts`: the six `compType*` keys in DE and FI; `check_copy_gate.py` (or a sibling) checks every `label_i18n_key` in `competition_types.csv` against all three locales.
4. Wireframe and overview corrected to #128.
5. Evidence from the dev server: 48 links per language, the groups visible after a background load, the DE/FI labels present.

**Not in scope:** #57, #69, the competition page itself (#129), the footer link (#127).

<details>
<summary>Exploration detail — for the builder and the reviewers, not required reading</summary>

- The row is a `<div class="comp-row">` today; Home's `HeroFixtures.astro` already links to `/{lang}/{competition_slug}/` through `localeHref`, and `[competition]/index.astro` builds one page per row of `competition_index.json`, so every slug on this page has a page.
- The collapse defect: `applyEmptyCategoryCollapse()` tests `r.offsetParent !== null`; in a tab that is not rendered every row reports `null`, so all eight groups get `hidden`. Observed 2026-09-14 in the Browser pane: `hidden: [true ×8]`, `visibleRows: 0` after a background load; `[false ×8]`, 48 after a reload in the foreground.
- `check_copy_gate.py` reports 477 strings across 3 locales and consults the corpus of keys the pages show; the six kinds are never shown today, so their missing DE/FI never fails. The guard must read the seed, not the pages.
- `08_browse.md` §7 describes `/football/{country-slug}/` country hubs, "still pending" per `00_overview.md` row 08; they are in no menu and no issue.
</details>

### #148 The current round as a warehouse fact: phase key + number on mart_competition_index, one row for the meta line

_opened · created 2026-09-14_

**Requested by:** Rami

The competition page's meta line is Country · Season · Matchday (CPO 2026-09-14, #129). Its three parts come from three places today and the third does not exist as a translatable fact: the round is the provider's English text (`Regular Season - 4`, `Round of 16`, `Clausura - 9`, `1/128-finals`, `League Phase - 1`). The CPO asked for a single source; the answer is one row per competition on `mart_competition_index`.

## What exactly

- [ ] `mart_competition_index` serves, per competition, the current round as a **phase key** and a **round number** (`current_round_phase_key`, `current_round_number`), derived in the warehouse from the round text of the competition's next matchday (`mart_next_matchday`); the page renders "Matchday 4" / "4. Spieltag" / "4. kierros" or "Round of 16" / "Achtelfinale" / "Neljännesvälierät" from site copy keyed on the phase.
- [ ] Every distinct round text in `fct_fixture` maps to a phase key (a seed of patterns → phase, e.g. `Regular Season - N` → `regular_season` + N, `Round of 16` → `round_of_16`, `Group Stage - N` → `group_stage` + N, `League Phase - N` → `league_phase` + N, `Quarter-finals` → `quarter_finals`, `Clausura - N` → `clausura` + N); a test fails on a round text no pattern covers, so a new format cannot render as English silently.
- [ ] The same row carries the season label (#105) and the region key (exists), so the meta line reads one source.
- [ ] Every phase key has EN/DE/FI copy, held by the copy gate's seed-key check.

## Why

The meta line is the first thing on every competition page; three sources for one line is how one of them drifts, and a round shown only in the provider's English on the German and Finnish pages is the defect #866 (GitHub-era) recorded for the fixture page.

## How

1. Measure the distinct round texts on `fct_fixture` (all competitions, all seasons) and group them by shape.
2. A seed `round_phases` (pattern, phase_key, has_number) and a base-or-intermediate model that resolves each fixture's round to (phase_key, number); a singular test that every round text resolves.
3. `mart_competition_index` joins the next matchday's phase and number; `mart_next_matchday` carries them per fixture too (the date headings and Home's block may use them later).
4. Site copy: one key per phase in three languages; the competition page renders the meta line from the served keys.

**Not in scope:** the season label itself (#105); the venue clock (#146).

<details>
<summary>Exploration detail — for the builder and the reviewers, not required reading</summary>

Round texts seen on `mart_next_matchday` 2026-09-14: `Regular Season - N` (leagues), `Clausura - 9` / `Apertura - 8` (Argentina, Mexico), `Championship Group - 24` (Finland's split), `Group Stage - 1`, `League Phase - 1`, `League Stage - 1`, `1st Preliminary Round`, `Round of 32`, `1st Round Qualifying Replays`, `Quarter-finals`, `1/128-finals`, plain `1` (Nations League). The provider is not consistent across competitions ("League Phase" vs "League Stage"), which is why the mapping is a seed and the test is strict.
</details>

### #152 Metric groups defined in one place: the catalogue's group key (duels → one_on_one) with names as copy in three languages and one order per group

_opened · created 2026-09-16_

**Requested by:** Rami

The metric catalogue is the single source of truth for every metric and its name. Its `metric_group` column carries a group key on every row, but the group itself is defined nowhere: no display name in any language, no order. The site hard-codes an English list of group names (`site_v2/src/lib/metricRows.ts`, `MetricGroup` / `GROUP_ORDER`), which is why group headings render in English on the German and Finnish pages (#98), and why the Rankings tab review on #129 found a group called "Duels" holding a board called "Duels" plus five dribbling metrics. Ruled by the CPO on 2026-09-16 during that review: **no second seed** — the catalogue keeps the assignment, the group's names are site copy keyed by the group key, the order is a catalogue column, and tests bind the three.

## What exactly

- [ ] **The group key `duels` becomes `one_on_one`** in `dbt_project/seeds/metric_catalogue.csv` (its 10 metrics: 2 team, 8 player, the dribble metrics included — a one-on-one is a duel or a dribble); every reader of the key follows (the site's group list, the seeds' `accepted_values`, the tests, the design-mocks generators).
- [ ] **Group display names as site copy, keyed by the group key** (`metricGroups.<key>.label`, the way `label_i18n_key` works for a metric), EN/DE/FI, held by the copy gate — the CPO's names:

| Key | EN | DE | FI |
|---|---|---|---|
| goals | Goals | Tore | Maalit |
| shooting | Shooting | Schüsse | Laukaukset |
| passing | Passing | Pässe | Syötöt |
| one_on_one | One-on-one | Eins-gegen-eins | Yksi vastaan yksi |
| defending | Defending | Defensive | Puolustus |
| discipline | Discipline | Disziplin | Kurinpito |
| goalkeeping | Goalkeeping | Torwart | Maalivahti |
| set_pieces | Set pieces | Standards | Erikoistilanteet |
| outcomes | Results | Ergebnisse | Tulokset |
| playing_time | Playing time | Einsatzzeit | Peliaika |

- [ ] **Group order in the catalogue:** a `metric_group_order` column, the same value on every row of a group; the order as the table above reads.
- [ ] **Tests:** every `metric_group` key has copy in all three languages; a group has exactly one order; no group key outside the set the copy knows. The hard-coded `MetricGroup` type and `GROUP_ORDER` in `metricRows.ts` go; the frontend reads the catalogue's key and order and the copy's names.
- [ ] Every surface that shows a group heading (the team and player page metric groups, the Rankings tab) reads them from there; #98 closes with this.

## Why

A heading named by hand in one language, on a page whose every number comes from a governed catalogue, is the one ungoverned thing on the page; it showed as a group named after one of its members and as English headings on German pages.

## How

1. Catalogue: rename the key, add the order column, the assignment unchanged otherwise (all 87 metrics checked on 2026-09-16: the only wrong bucket was dribbles under "duels", resolved by the group's new name, not by a move).
2. Copy: the ten keys in EN/DE/FI; the copy gate.
3. Tests and the frontend; the mock generators read the same.
4. `docs/metric_layer.md` records that a group is defined by its key in the catalogue, its names in copy and its order in the catalogue, nowhere else.

**Not in scope:** the Rankings tab's boards themselves (#151 and the player half's issue), which read the groups this issue defines.

### #153 One design language, held by a mechanism: the element inventory in the block standard, its CSS in one stylesheet, a cross-page check that measures every page

_closed · created 2026-09-16 · closed 2026-09-17_

**Requested by:** Rami

The competition page review (#129, 2026-09-16) changed six site-wide rules and introduced four elements, one page at a time, and each reached another page unseen (Home's boards, Home's hover, the Table's hover, the tab bar). The CPO's requirement: **one consistent design language, held by a mechanism, so no page is ever re-checked by eye** — "if we build the next page type you break things hidden somewhere else, and then I have to cross-check another page, every element, every title font size, content block."

## What exactly

- [ ] **One inventory of the site's elements, in the block standard (the design chain's document), each with its rule and its measurements**, and its CSS in `site_v2/src/styles/system.css` only: the block heading (13px capitals; 14px from its rule to the block's first line, nothing added by the content); the level-1 group heading (17px bold, 34px above, no rule when used inside a block); the table (head row with column labels, or the table's name for a single-value table, the head rule the only line; striped rows counted from the head, first plain; one fixed track list per table kind); the board as a single-value table (rank · crest name · value, the player's club under the name, five rows on a competition page, seven on Home); the match row and its date heading; the fact row (value in the accent); the tag (Next, Top match); the matchday picker; the chevron heading link; the ordered-by number (bold 15px accent, everywhere); the one hover tint for every row link (visible against a stripe) and the press tint; the tab bar (fits its tabs in one row at 375px in three languages); every title at the block's left edge, whatever its level. **A page has no styling of its own; it composes elements.** An element not in the inventory is a design decision, put to the CPO and rendered on every page it touches before it is ruled.
- [ ] **A cross-page check that fails the build**: every design-mock generator and every built page type is rendered at 375px and 700px in EN and FI and measured against the inventory — heading gaps, title left edges, stripe start, hover tint, font sizes, the ordered-by number's colour, tab-bar fit, the 14px rule; one page breaking while another is worked on turns the check red. Runs in `validate:ui` on every MR.
- [ ] **A guard on page-specific CSS**: a lint that fails a page or component stylesheet that restyles an inventory selector (the class list above) outside `system.css`.
- [ ] **The render naming rule** for review mocks, in `design-mocks/README.md`: `<page>_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<nn>.html`, the number counting up per page and never reset; a render sent for review is never overwritten.
- [ ] The four renders of 2026-09-16 (`competition-overview`, `competition-matchdays`, `competition-rankings`, `home`, all `_2026-09-16_01`) and their generators (`gen_competition_matchdays.py`, `gen_competition_teams.py`, `gen_overview_after_teams.py`, `gen_home_with_rules.py`, in the session scratchpad) brought into `design-mocks/` as the first content the check measures.

## Why

Rules ruled on one page and applied by hand are how the site drifts: the hover tint, the stripe start, the title edge and the tab-bar fit were each found broken on a page nobody was looking at. A page built from an inventory that a check measures cannot drift silently, and the CPO stops re-checking pages by eye.

## How

Decided at planning (2026-09-16, in chat): the check measures pages in **headless Chromium via Playwright for Python** on Microsoft's ready image (no browser exists in CI today; every current check is a regex over HTML); **review renders are tracked in git** under `design-mocks/renders/`. Found at planning: no block-standard document exists in the design chain (only #50 and `gen_block_standard.py`), so the inventory creates one.

1. **The renders of record, tracked** (item 4): `design-mocks/renders/`, the four `_2026-09-16_01` files moved in; `design-mocks/render.py` picks the next `<page>_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<nn>` and refuses an existing name; a test enforces the pattern and the contiguous numbering; the README carries the rule.
2. **The inventory, one stylesheet, the lint, the measured check** (items 1–3, run locally): first the two open rulings rendered on every page they touch and put to the CPO one at a time — (a) the level-1 group heading's rule when used inside a block (Home's approved render has it, the Rankings render does not), (b) row lines on a table besides the head rule (the approved Overview has them, this issue's text says the head rule is the only line). Then `docs/wireframes/block_standard.md` (the inventory: every element with selector, rule, "Measured as" and status; the pages list), added to the design chain's reading order; `system.css` consolidated and every per-page or per-mock CSS rule removed (`ROW_CSS`, `INTERACTION_CSS`, the board `MOCK_CSS`, the four overlays' CSS); `CompetitionTabs.astro` to the approved three tabs, or the built Overview fails the tab-bar measurement; `scripts/design_inventory.py` (the parser), `scripts/check_page_css.py` (the lint), `scripts/check_design_inventory.py` (the measured check: 375 and 700, EN and FI, one failure line per element), `tests/test_design_inventory.py` with a RED fixture reconstructing the defects of 2026-09-16.
3. **The check in CI** (a protected file): `build:site-v2` keeps `dist/` as an artifact; `validate:ui` runs on the Playwright image, needs the build, runs the lint, the tests and the check on every MR that touches `site_v2/**`, `design-mocks/**` or the inventory.
4. #150 and #151 do not merge until the check passes on their pages and on Home.

**Not in scope:** any new element or rule (each is a CPO decision on its page's issue, rendered on every page it touches first).

The audit's check 5 fails the build on each.
- [ ] The wording of the corrected title is the CPO's (user-visible copy, all three languages), put on the MR that changes it; the competition and the date are the two facts that tell the meetings apart, both served on the fixture payload.
- [ ] `node scripts/audit-seo.mjs site_v2/dist` is clean on a build that carries every unplayed match (`check-built-pages` proves the count: 5,022 on 2026-09-19).

## Why

The build with every unplayed match (15,078 match pages, 5,022 fixtures x 3 locales) fails `audit-seo` on exactly 36 violations, all of them this: 12 pairings x 3 locales. Nothing else at full scale is red: the heap holds at the deploy job's 8 GB (14 minutes), and the page-count check passes. The committed sample never showed it because no two sample matches share a pairing.

## How

1. The fixture page's title (and its description, if it repeats the same two names) gains the two distinguishing facts; the copy for EN/DE/FI is drafted and put to the CPO on the MR.
2. `audit-seo.test.mjs` pins that two pairings on different dates or competitions produce distinct titles.
3. A full-scale build (the deploy export, then `astro build` with the deploy job's heap) is run once and `audit-seo` is green.

**Not in scope:** the match page's content (#132 reviews it); the Matchdays tab (#150), whose page-count check is what surfaced this.

## 4 · Teams

### #114 Top teams: a real tie-break for equal per-match rates, instead of an arbitrary key

_opened · created 2026-09-09_

When two teams share the top per-match rate in a league on a Home Top teams board, nothing meaningful separates them and the mart falls back to team_sk, which is stable and means nothing. CPO 2026-09-09: no criterion for now, revisit later.

WHY THERE IS NO OBVIOUS ANSWER, and why the player rule does not transfer:

The player boards break a tie on FEWER MINUTES PLAYED - the same goal tally in less time is a real performance claim. Teams have no minutes analogue. The nearest field, season_games_played, was proposed and rejected, correctly, for two reasons:

- It barely discriminates. Measured across 235 league-seasons: 3.6 distinct game counts per league-season on average, and in 72 of them every team has played exactly the same number.
- More fundamentally it asserts the wrong thing. For a RATE, fewer games does not mean better, it means less evidence for the same rate. Fewer minutes for an equal goal tally is efficiency; fewer games for an equal goals-per-match is just a smaller sample.

SCALE: 2 of 259 league-board-seasons currently carry a tie, so this is rare - but rare is not never, and the board claims one team per league.

DIRECTIONS WORTH MEASURING BEFORE PICKING ONE:
- a second board metric as a secondary sort (for goals_per_match, perhaps shots on goal per match), accepting that it mixes two measures
- the underlying total rather than the rate, which only helps when games played differ
- showing the tied teams together rather than picking, which breaks the one-team-per-league rule and therefore needs its own ruling
- keeping the arbitrary key but making the tie visible to the reader

Sibling of #112, which asks the same question for the player boards where the last resort is player_sk. Whatever answer is found may serve both, or may not - the player boards are integer counts and the team boards are rates, which is exactly why the tie rates differ so much (12 of 28 league-boards tie on the player side).

Priority: LOW. Current behaviour is correct, deterministic and honestly labelled in the model.

## 5 · Players

### #42 Pass accuracy reads 23-30% since 2022 against 72-73% before (re-filed from the unreachable GitHub #841)

_opened · created 2026-08-10_

Pass accuracy reads **23–30% from 2022 onward, against 72–73% before it**. A 72% pass accuracy is
normal for a football team; 25% is not physically plausible. The number is wrong, not merely odd.

⚠ **This was filed once already, on the GitHub tracker as #841.** That tracker did not migrate and
is unreachable, so this re-files it on GitLab. It is NOT a new discovery.

## Why this is being re-filed now

It was dropped from the **Top teams** home block (#41) when that block went to one metric per
board, and dropping it from one surface fixed nothing: **the number will still be shown elsewhere**
— the team stats page and the player stats page both carry pass accuracy. Removing a broken metric
from one block only changes where it surfaces. It has to be fixed.

## Two metrics, two formulas — and they are not the same

From `dbt_project/seeds/metric_catalogue.csv`:

| metric_id | entity | numerator | denominator |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pass_accuracy` | team | `sum(passes_accurate)` | `sum(passes_total)` |
| `pass_accuracy_pct` | player | `sum(cast(round(passes_total * passes_accuracy_percent / 100.0) as int64))` | `sum(passes_total)` |

The team metric divides a **raw provider count**. The player metric **reconstructs** the accurate
count from the provider's own percentage field, then divides.

⚠ **Hypothesis, NOT verified** — nothing here has been run against BigQuery, because warehouse work
is paused while CI minutes are exhausted. The shape of the defect fits `passes_accurate` having
changed or stopped being populated for team fixtures from 2022, which would corrupt the team metric
while leaving the player one intact, since the player one never reads that column. **Verify before
acting on it.** A fix built on this without checking would be guesswork.

## What to check first

1. **Is it team-only, or both?** If `pass_accuracy_pct` (player) reads sane over the same seasons
   while `pass_accuracy` (team) does not, the fault is in `passes_accurate`, not in the concept.
2. **Is `passes_accurate` NULL, zero, or a different unit after 2022?** A NULL summing to 0 against
   a healthy denominator produces exactly this kind of collapse. Check the RAW table, not staging —
   staging keeps only the latest payload and will mask ingested history.
3. **Does the provider still populate the field**, or has the endpoint's shape changed? If the
   column is simply gone, the team formula has to move to the percentage-based one the player
   metric already uses, and that is a metric-definition change, not a bug fix.
4. **Which surfaces render it today**, so the blast radius is known before anything changes.

## Why it matters beyond one number

- The user cannot manually verify numbers, so a plausible-looking wrong value is worse than a
  missing one. Data quality is non-negotiable in this project.
- The two entities disagreeing on formula for a metric that shares a display name is a problem in
  its own right. If both are meant to be "accurate passes over total passes", they should not be
  computed two ways — and if they genuinely differ, they should not share the label.

## Not in scope here

The fix itself is not scoped until step 1 answers whether this is a data defect, an ingestion
defect, or a metric-definition problem. Those land in different layers.

## Blocked by

GitLab CI minutes are exhausted (`ci_quota_exceeded`) and warehouse work is paused, so none of the
checks above can be run yet.

### #99 Step 4: the export reads player goals/assists by the OLD key via .get() — silent null-out

_opened · created 2026-08-29_

Found while scoping the sample refresh after batch F (!123).

`scripts/export_site_data.py` reads two catalogue PLAYER metrics by literal key, in two places, with `.get()` and no default:

- `_shape_squad_member` (:192-193) — `career.get("goals")`, `career.get("assists")` -> the team page Squad tab
- the career-row shaper (:443-444) — `row.get("goals")`, `row.get("assists")` -> the player payload

Both read `mart_player_career`, whose own header comment says it plainly (`mart_player_career.sql:128-130`): "`goals` and `assists` are both catalogue rows (entity=player, group=goals, tier 1)".

Step 4 renames them `goals -> goals_player` and `assists -> assists_player` (the 35-row PLAYER list in escalations.log, block THE METRIC CATALOGUE NAMING PROGRAMME). After that rename `.get()` returns `None` for every row — no KeyError, no exception, no test failure — and the payload keys stay `"goals"`/`"assists"` while their VALUES all become null.

That is not honest absence; it is a broken binding wearing absence's clothes. The Squad tab shows only members with >= 1 appearance, so the columns would render empty for everyone.

Fix, when step 4 runs: move both read keys with the rename. The payload keys themselves are a separate question — they are display-layer names, not catalogue ids, and the recorded rule is that a metric and its column may legitimately differ.

Also worth a guard: nothing offline pins these four literals to the mart columns they read.

### #112 Top players: a meaningful last-resort tie-break, not player_sk

_opened · created 2026-09-09_

When two players are level at the top of a league on a Home board, the tie is broken by fewer minutes played (CPO ruling 2026-09-09, recorded in .claude/task/escalations.log). That settles almost all of it, but not all.

Measured against prod on 2026-09-09, over the 28 league-boards the Home Top players block renders:
- 12 carry a tie
- fewer minutes resolves 11 of them
- 1 survives both the value and the minutes comparison

That survivor currently falls to player_sk, which is stable and completely meaningless. It is implemented in mart_leaderboards.league_leader_order and is LABELLED as meaningless in the column description, the model comment and the ruling itself, so nothing is pretending otherwise. It is honest, deterministic and unsatisfying.

What is wanted: a last resort that means something in football terms, or a display treatment that does not have to pick at all.

Directions worth MEASURING before choosing between them:
- a secondary sporting criterion (appearances, or a contribution measure related to the board itself)
- showing the joint leaders together rather than picking one, which breaks the one-per-league rule set on 2026-08-18 and therefore needs a CPO ruling
- keeping the arbitrary key but making the tie visible to the reader rather than hidden

Priority: MINOR. The current behaviour is correct and not a defect; this is about making the last step meaningful.

Related: mart_leaderboards.league_leader_order, dbt_project/tests/assert_mart_leaderboards_one_leader_per_league.sql, MR !164.

The roadmap is the site's menu, in order, each hub before the pages behind it, and every page rechecked by the CPO — built or not — because the earlier agreements may be stale and a built page is not a proof it can be built to the current design. One issue per page is the single place where its design, its data sources and its links are agreed.
